questions.question:
Solution: Turn on ingress, create a custom scale rule, and apply that rule to the container app.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Container Apps requires either ingress, a minimum replica count, or a custom scale rule to avoid an app with disabled ingress becoming unable to start after scaling to zero. Enabling ingress permits users to reach the app, while the custom scale rule supplies a scaling trigger that can activate replicas. [Scaling in Azure Container Apps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)\
\
**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

questions.question:
Solution: Turn on ingress and set the container app's minimum replica count to 1.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Container Apps requires ingress to expose an app to incoming traffic. A minimum replica setting of 1 keeps at least one revision replica running instead of allowing the app to scale to zero, restoring availability for users.\
\
**Learn more:** [Ingress in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/ingress-overview) · [Set scaling rules in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

questions.question:
Solution: Turn on ingress, create an HTTP scale rule, and apply that rule to the container app.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Container Apps with ingress disabled can scale to zero and have no HTTP-based way to start again. Enabling ingress makes the app reachable for HTTP traffic, while an HTTP scale rule uses incoming request concurrency to scale the app out from zero. [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)\
\
**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

questions.question:
Solution: Enable ingress, create a TCP scale rule, and apply that rule to the container app.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Enabling ingress makes the container app reachable, and a TCP scaling rule can trigger replicas from incoming TCP connections even when the revision has scaled to zero. Azure Container Apps documents TCP scaling with `minReplicas` set to `0` and ingress configured for TCP traffic.\
\
**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app) · [Configure Ingress for your app in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/ingress-how-to)

You must create the project in either Python or C# without using a template.  
  
You need to specify the command and its parameter required to create the Azure Functions app project.  
  
Which command and parameter should you specify?

<Dropdown

/>","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a web application that uses Azure Cache for Redis. You expect the cache to fill frequently and will need to evict keys.  
  
You must configure Azure Cache for Redis for the following predicted usage pattern: a small subset of elements will be accessed much more often than the remaining elements.  
  
You need to configure Azure Cache for Redis to optimize performance for the predicted usage pattern.  
  
Which two eviction policies will meet the goal?  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
LRU eviction preserves frequently accessed keys by removing the keys that have gone unused for the longest time. `allkeys-lru` evaluates all keys, whereas `volatile-lru` evaluates keys that have an expiration set. Both therefore favor the frequently accessed subset under memory pressure.

**Learn more:** [Configure Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-configure) · [Best practices for memory management - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-best-practices-memory-management)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],This question requires you to assess the underlined text to determine whether it is correct.  
  
Your company has an on-premises deployment of MongoDB and an Azure Cosmos DB account that uses the MongoDB API.  
  
You need to devise a strategy to migrate MongoDB to the Azure Cosmos DB account.  
  
You include the Data Management Gateway tool in your migration strategy.  
  
Instructions: Review the underlined text. If it makes the statement correct, select `No change required.` If the statement is incorrect, select the answer choice that makes the statement correct.
questions.explanation:
`mongorestore` is a MongoDB native tool that restores BSON data into a MongoDB-compatible destination, including Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB. It is appropriate for migrating an on-premises MongoDB deployment after creating a dump with `mongodump`.

**Learn more:** [Premigration steps for data migrations from MongoDB to Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/pre-migration-steps)

You are building an Azure Web App and configure TLS mutual authentication for it.  
  
You need to validate the client certificate in the web app.

<Dropdown
  blanks={[{"id":"client_certificate_location","options":["HTTP request header","Client cookie","HTTP message body","URL query string"],"answer":"HTTP request header","label":"Client certificate location"},{"id":"encoding_type","options":["HTML","URL","Unicode","Base64"],"answer":"Base64","label":"Encoding type"}]}

/>","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an inventory-tracking solution. The solution contains an Azure Function app with multiple functions that are triggered by Azure Cosmos DB. You plan to deploy the solution across multiple Azure regions.  
  
The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Item results from Azure Cosmos DS must return the latest committed version of an item.  
- Items written to Azure Cosmos DB must guarantee ordering.  
  
You need to configure the consistency level for the Azure Cosmos DB deployments.  
  
Which consistency level should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB strong consistency provides linearizability: reads always return the most recently committed item version, and committed writes are globally ordered. The weaker consistency levels can return stale data or provide ordering guarantees only within more limited bounds or sessions.

**Learn more:** [Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels)

questions.question:
You are developing an ASP.NET Core website that uses Azure FrontDoor. The website builds custom weather data sets for researchers. Users download the data sets as Comma Separated Value (CSV) files, and the data is refreshed every 10 hours.  
  
Specific files must be purged from the FrontDoor cache according to Response Header values.  
  
You need to purge individual assets from the Front Door cache. Which type of cache purge should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door uses a single-path purge to remove an individual cached asset by specifying the asset’s full path, including its file extension. Wildcard purges target groups of files and folders, and a root-domain purge clears all assets for the endpoint.\
\
**Learn more:** [Purge cache in Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/cache-purge)

questions.question:
Proposed solution: Configure an Azure Monitor Insights workbook.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor workbooks provide interactive analysis and visual reports; they do not define alert-response automation. Azure Monitor action groups can invoke an Azure Function when an alert fires, so an action group with a Function action is required to execute Function1.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups) · [Azure Workbooks overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/visualize/workbooks-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure Application Insights Smart Detection.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Application Insights Smart Detection identifies potential performance and failure anomalies, but it does not by itself configure an existing alert to execute an Azure Function. An Azure Monitor action group with an Azure Function action must be associated with the alert rule to invoke Function1 when the alert fires.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Monitor action groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups) · [Smart detection in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/proactive-diagnostics)

questions.question:
Solution: Set up an Azure Monitor action group.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor action groups can be associated with alert rules and include Azure Function actions. An alert firing can therefore invoke Function1 in addition to sending its email notification.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure an Application Insights funnel.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Application Insights funnel is an analytics feature for examining conversion through a sequence of user actions; it does not execute an Azure Function in response to an alert. Azure Monitor action groups support automated actions, including calling an existing HTTP-triggered Azure Function, when an alert fires.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

Solution: Configure an Application Insights funnel.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Functions Premium supports virtual network connectivity and private endpoints for secure access to protected resources, while retaining event-driven scaling. An App Service plan uses dedicated capacity and is billed even when the function is idle; the legacy Consumption plan is pay-per-execution but does not support virtual network integration or private endpoints. Therefore, Premium is the appropriate balance of the required security capabilities and cost-efficient scaling.

**Learn more:** [Azure Functions scale and hosting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-scale) · [Azure Functions Premium plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-premium-plan)

options.text: Remove the role assignment for the security principle.

questions.explanation:
A user delegation SAS can be revoked by revoking its user delegation key, which invalidates SAS tokens signed with that key. It can also be revoked by changing or removing the RBAC role assignment for the security principal used to create the SAS, because Azure Storage verifies that principal’s required permissions when the SAS is used. Stored access policies and storage account-key regeneration do not revoke a user delegation SAS.

**Learn more:** [Create a user delegation SAS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-user-delegation-sas)

questions.question:
Solution: Include Azure Redis Cache in the design.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cache for Redis is an in-memory cache whose data resides in the selected Azure region by default. Although supported tiers can provide high availability and geo-replication, an application must explicitly use regional cache instances and route clients to an appropriate endpoint; Redis Cache alone does not provide geographically nearest content delivery for streaming users.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Cache for Redis planning FAQs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-planning-faq) · [High availability for Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-high-availability)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
Solution: You add an Azure Content Delivery Network (CDN) to the design.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Content Delivery Network caches publicly available content on edge servers close to end users, reducing latency and origin load. It supports on-demand video streaming and improves delivery performance and availability for geographically distributed users.\
\
**Learn more:** [CDN guidance - Azure Architecture Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/best-practices/cdn)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
Solution: You incorporate a Storage Area Network (SAN) into your design.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: A SAN provides centralized block-level storage, but it does not inherently deliver streaming content from locations nearest to users or provide the global distribution and delivery capabilities needed for a consistent, highly available video-streaming experience.

You are building a solution that will use Azure messaging services.  
  
You need to ensure that the solution uses a publish-subscribe model and removes the need for constant polling.  
  
Which two approaches could achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus topics and subscriptions provide durable one-to-many publish/subscribe messaging. Azure Event Grid is a managed publish-subscribe service that can push events to subscribers when state changes occur, avoiding constant polling. Event Hubs consumers use a pull model, while queues use point-to-point messaging.

**Learn more:** [Service Bus queues, topics, and subscriptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-queues-topics-subscriptions) · [What is Azure Event Grid?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an Azure App Service web app.  
  
The web app must securely store session data in Azure Redis Cache.  
  
You need to connect the web app to Azure Redis Cache.  
  
Which three Azure Redis Cache properties should you use? Each correct answer forms part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A secure Azure Cache for Redis client connection requires the cache host name, the TLS/SSL port, and an access key for authentication. Subscription metadata and location are Azure resource-management attributes, not connection settings.

**Learn more:** [Use redis-cli - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-how-to-redis-cli-tool) · [TLS configuration settings - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-tls-configuration)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop an ASP. Net Care application by integrating the Application Insights SDK into your solution.  
  
The application sends telemetry at a very high rate over a short interval. You observe fewer events, traces, and metrics being recorded, along with increased telemetry-ingestion error rates. Telemetry data must synchronize client and server information to enable HTTP request and response correlation.  
  
You need to reduce telemetry traffic, data costs, and storage costs while maintaining a statistically accurate analysis of application telemetry data.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set a daily cap on the Log Analytics workspace. Create an Activity log alert rule.
Modify the pricing tier for the Log Analytics workspace.
Update the application code to reduce the number of DiagnosticSource events. Use filtering to exclude these events.
Disable adaptive sampling. Enable and configure the fixed-rate sampling module.

questions.explanation:
Fixed-rate sampling reduces telemetry volume before ingestion while retaining a representative fraction of the data for statistically valid analysis. A consistent sampling decision across the telemetry in a trace preserves correlated request, response, and related telemetry; Application Insights can account for the sampling rate when reporting counts. Source-level sampling also reduces ingestion and storage costs, unlike changing a workspace tier or applying a daily cap.

**Learn more:** [Sampling in Azure Application Insights with OpenTelemetry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/opentelemetry-sampling) · [Application Insights FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-my/azure/azure-monitor/app/application-insights-faq)

You need to verify the availability of the corporate website.  
  
Which two test types can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Custom testing using the TrackAvailability API method

questions.explanation:
Application Insights Standard availability tests can validate TLS/SSL certificate validity and send custom HTTP headers. A custom availability test can run application-defined test logic and submit its result to Application Insights by using `TrackAvailability()`. URL ping tests are deprecated, and multi-step web tests are not a current supported availability-test type.\
\
**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

You have a Standard-tier Azure Cache for Redis instance named `redis1` that uses the default configuration.  
  
You need to configure a Maxmemory policy to increase the cache capacity available for read operations.  
  
How should you configure the Maxmemory policy?

options.text: Set the Maxmemory policy to noeviction.
Set the Maxmemory policy to volatile-lru.

questions.explanation:
`maxmemory-reserved` is memory reserved for non-cache operations, such as replication during failover, and is unavailable for cached data. Decreasing that reservation increases the memory available to store cache entries. Maxmemory eviction policies control which keys are removed when the cache reaches its memory limit; they do not increase the amount of memory available for cached data.

**Learn more:** [How to configure Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-configure) · [Best practices for memory management - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-best-practices-memory-management)

questions.question:
You are using PowerShell to create an Azure key vault. Deleted objects in the key vault must be retained for a specified period of 90 days.  
  
Which two parameters must be used together to satisfy this requirement? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Soft delete retains deleted Azure Key Vault objects for the retention period, and purge protection prevents their permanent deletion during that period. Purge protection depends on soft delete; deployment and template-deployment settings do not control deleted-object retention.\
\
**Learn more:** [New-AzKeyVault (Az.KeyVault)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.keyvault/new-azkeyvault?view=azps-15.3.0) · [Update-AzKeyVault (Az.KeyVault)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.keyvault/update-azkeyvault?view=azps-15.6.0)

questions.question:
Solution: Use Blob storage events to trigger photo processing.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage events are delivered through Azure Event Grid for near-real-time event-driven processing. General-purpose v2 storage accounts support Event Grid integration, and image processing is a documented Blob Storage event scenario.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reacting to Azure Blob storage events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-event-overview) · [Azure Blob Storage as an Event Grid source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-schema-blob-storage)

questions.question:
Solution: Change the Azure Storage account to a BlockBlobStorage storage account.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Changing a General-purpose v2 account to a BlockBlobStorage account does not provide a mechanism to detect photo uploads and initiate image processing within one minute. Azure Storage account types also cannot be changed in place to a different type; moving to another type requires creating a new account and copying data. [Azure Storage account overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview)\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Storage account overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview)

questions.question:
Proposed solution: Move the photo-processing workload to an Azure Function that is triggered by the blob upload.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A standard Azure Blob Storage trigger uses polling and does not guarantee that processing begins within one minute after a blob upload. A lower-latency event-based trigger, such as the Event Grid-based Blob trigger, would be required to meet a sub-minute start requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Blob storage trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-storage-blob-trigger) · [Respond to blob storage events using Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/scenario-blob-storage-events)

questions.question:
Solution: Create an Azure Function app that uses the Consumption hosting model and is triggered by the blob upload.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The default polling-based Blob Storage trigger on an Azure Functions Consumption plan can delay processing of a new blob by up to 10 minutes after the function app becomes idle. It therefore cannot ensure that photo processing starts within one minute; an event-based Blob trigger using Event Grid provides lower latency.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Blob storage trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-storage-blob-trigger) · [Storage considerations for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/storage-considerations)

questions.question:
Solution: Use the Azure Blob Storage change feed to initiate photo processing.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage change-feed records become available within a few minutes of a change, rather than providing a sub-minute trigger. It therefore cannot ensure that photo processing starts in less than one minute.\
\
**Learn more:** [Change feed support in Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-change-feed)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Linux container-based console application that uploads image files from customer sites worldwide. A back-end system running on Azure virtual machines processes the images by using the Azure Blobs API.  
  
You aren't allowed to modify the application.  
  
Some customer sites have only phone-based internet connections.  
  
You need to configure the console application to access the images.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Azure Storage Network File System (NFS) 3.0 support

questions.explanation:
Azure BlobFuse mounts an Azure Blob Storage container as a file system in Linux and translates file-system operations into Azure Blob REST API calls. This lets an unchanged Linux application work with the blob-based image store over HTTPS, without requiring SMB or NFS connectivity.

**Learn more:** [What is BlobFuse? - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/blobfuse2-what-is) · [Mount an Azure Blob Storage container on Linux with BlobFuse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/blobfuse2-how-to-deploy)

questions.question:
You need to retain the user agreements.  
  
Where should you store an agreement once it has been completed?
questions.explanation: Azure Storage queues durably hold messages until a consumer retrieves and processes them, making them suitable for retaining a completed agreement for asynchronous downstream handling.

questions.question:
You need to address the capacity issue.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Convert the trigger on the Azure Function to an Azure Blob storage trigger
Ensure that the consumption plan is configured correctly to allow scaling
Move the Azure Function to a dedicated App Service Plan
Update the loop starting on line PC09 to process items in parallel

questions.explanation:
Parallel processing enables independent items to be handled concurrently, increasing the Azure Function’s throughput and relieving a bottleneck caused by sequential loop execution. Azure Functions supports concurrent processing, and concurrency directly affects throughput and scale behavior.\
\
**Learn more:** [Concurrency in Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-concurrency)

questions.question:
You need to address the capacity issue.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
AzCopy copies data between Azure storage accounts and can be incorporated into automated scripts. It creates a job plan and log files for each job; a failed or canceled job can be resumed using its job ID, which makes the transfer recoverable.

**Learn more:** [Get started with AzCopy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-use-azcopy-v10) · [Find errors and resume jobs with logs in AzCopy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-use-azcopy-configure)

You administer an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL API account named account1. The account includes a database named db1, which contains a container named container1. You configure account1 to use session consistency.  
  
You plan to develop an application named App1 that accesses container1. Individual App1 instances must perform both reads and writes. App1 must enable multiple nodes to participate in the same session.  
  
You need to configure an object that shares the session token among the nodes.  
  
Which object should you use?
questions.explanation:
Session consistency uses a session token generated by writes. Multiple application nodes can participate in one session by propagating that token and setting it on subsequent requests through `RequestOptions.SessionToken`; this preserves read-your-own-writes behavior when a later request is handled by another node.

**Learn more:** [Manage consistency in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/nosql/how-to-manage-consistency) · [RequestOptions.SessionToken Property](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.azure.documents.client.requestoptions.sessiontoken?view=azure-dotnet)

You are developing a user portal for a company.  
  
You need to create a portal report that lists information about employees who are subject-matter experts on a specific topic. You must ensure that administrators retain full control over, and consent to, the data.  
  
Which technology should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Graph Data Connect provides a granular control and consent model for Microsoft 365 data. Administrators can review and approve applications and the specific datasets, columns, scopes, and destination permitted for access, making it appropriate for a governed employee-information reporting scenario.

You have a public-facing, on-premises website named www.contoso.com.  
  
You plan to use Application Insights availability tests to test the availability of www.contoso.com.  
  
You need to configure a test that generates HTTP POST requests with custom headers. The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
Which type of test should you configure?
questions.explanation:
A Standard availability test supports HTTP request verbs including POST, custom headers, and custom request data. It can be configured without writing and maintaining the custom code required for a Custom TrackAvailability test, minimizing development effort.\
\
**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

options.text: Create a user-assigned managed identity and assign role-based access controls.
Create an Azure AD custom role and assign the role to the Azure Blob storage account.
Create an Azure Key Vault and issue a client certificate.
Create a system-assigned managed identity and issue a client certificate.
Create an Azure AD custom role and assign role-based access controls.

questions.explanation:
A user-assigned managed identity is independent of the Logic App resource lifecycle, so deleting the Logic App does not automatically delete the identity in Microsoft Entra ID. Assigning the identity an appropriate Azure RBAC role on the Blob storage account grants secure, credential-free access to the storage resource.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate workflow connections to protected Azure resources by using managed identities in Azure Logic Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/logic-apps/authenticate-with-managed-identity) · [Securing managed identities in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/service-accounts-managed-identities)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an e-Commerce web app.  
  
You want to use Azure Key Vault to make sure that sign-ins to the e-Commerce web app are protected by using Azure App Service authentication and Azure Active Directory (AAD).  
  
What should you do on the e-Commerce web app?

options.text: Run the az keyvault secret command.
Create an Azure AD service principal.

questions.explanation:
A managed identity gives an Azure App Service app an automatically managed Microsoft Entra identity that can authenticate to Azure Key Vault without embedding or rotating credentials. Granting that identity the required Key Vault secret permission lets the app securely retrieve its sign-in-related secrets.

**Learn more:** [Use managed identities for App Service and Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-managed-identity) · [Use Key Vault references as app settings in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-key-vault-references)

questions.question:
You develop applications that integrate with a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You plan to implement a permission classification within the tenant.  
  
You need to choose permissions to include in the classification.  
  
Which permissions should you choose?

options.text: app-only access permissions that require admin consent
delegated permissions that require only user consent
app-only access permissions that require only user consent
delegated permissions that require admin consent

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra permission classifications apply only to delegated permissions that do not require administrator consent. These classifications support tenant consent policies that govern which permissions users may consent to.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure permission classifications - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-permission-classifications)

questions.question:
You need to examine the HTTP server log output to resolve the issue with the ContentUploadService.  
  
Which command should you use first?
questions.explanation:
`az container attach` attaches to a container in an Azure Container Instances container group and streams its standard output and standard error to the local console, providing the application-level diagnostic output needed to investigate an HTTP server issue.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure CLI az container attach](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/container?view=azure-cli-latest) · [Get container instance logs and events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-get-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a .NET Core MVC application that lets customers research independent holiday accommodation providers.  
  
You want to implement Azure Search so that the application can search the index with various criteria to find documents relating to accommodation.  
  
You want the application to let customers search the index by using regular expressions.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure the SearchMode property of the SearchParameters class.
Configure the QueryType property of the SearchParameters class.
Configure the Facets property of the SearchParameters class.
Configure the Filter property of the SearchParameters class.

questions.explanation:
Regular-expression searches in Azure AI Search require the full Lucene query syntax. Set the `QueryType` property to use the full query parser; `SearchMode`, `Facets`, and `Filter` do not enable regular-expression syntax.

**Learn more:** [Lucene query syntax in Azure AI Search](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/query-lucene-syntax)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that includes a resource group named RG1 and a Service Bus queue named SB1.  
  
You plan to implement an Azure Event Grid push event subscription that delivers an event to SB1 whenever a resource in RG1 is created, modified, or deleted. You must minimize development and configuration effort.  
  
You need to create an Event Grid topic for the planned implementation.  
  
Which event topic type should you create?
questions.explanation:
Azure resource groups are supported Azure Event Grid system-topic sources, and their resource-change events are published by Azure. A system topic therefore provides the required source without building a custom event publisher, while an Event Grid event subscription can directly deliver events to a Service Bus queue.

**Learn more:** [System topics in Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/system-topics) · [Azure resource group as an Event Grid source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-schema-resource-groups)

questions.question:
You intend to deploy an Azure Container App.  
  
You need to configure the container app to support session affinity.  
  
Which ingress type and revision mode should you assign to the container app?

options.text: HTTP ingress type and multiple revision mode
HTTP ingress type and single revision mode
TCP ingress type and multiple revision mode
TCP ingress type and single revision mode

questions.explanation:
Azure Container Apps session affinity (sticky sessions) is cookie-based and is supported only when HTTP ingress is enabled and the app uses single revision mode.\
\
**Learn more:** [Session Affinity in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/sticky-sessions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing several APIs hosted by Azure API Management (APIM).  
  
You must make several minor, non-breaking changes to one of the APIs. The API changes must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Must not disrupt API callers.  
- Enable rollback if issues are found.  
- Be documented so developers can understand what is new.  
- Be tested before publishing.  
  
You need to update the API.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure and apply a custom policy.
Add a new revision to the API.
Configure and apply query string-based versioning.

questions.explanation:
Azure API Management revisions support controlled, non-breaking changes without disrupting callers of the current revision. A revision can be edited and tested before it becomes current, published with a change-log entry for developers, and rolled back by making an earlier revision current. [Revisions in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-revisions)

**Learn more:** [Revisions in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-revisions) · [Tutorial: Use revisions in API Management for safe nonbreaking API changes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-get-started-revise-api)

questions.question:
You develop and deploy an Azure App Service web app in a production environment. You enable the Always On setting and the Application Insights site extensions.  
  
You deploy a code update and observe multiple failed requests and exceptions in the web app.  
  
You need to validate the web app's performance and failure counts in near real time.  
  
Which Application Insights tool should you use?
questions.explanation:
Application Insights Live Metrics Stream delivers near-real-time telemetry for a running web application, including performance metrics, failed-request counts, and exceptions. It is specifically suited to validating a deployed update while observing performance and failure counts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Live Metrics: Real-Time Monitoring in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/live-stream)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a data-processing application that receives requests from an Azure Storage queue.  
  
You need to control access to the queue and must meet these requirements:  
  
- Provide other applications with access to the Azure queue.  
- Ensure you can revoke access to the queue without regenerating the storage account keys.  
- Specify access at the queue level rather than at the storage account level.  
  
Which type of shared access signature (SAS) should you use?

options.text: Service SAS with a stored access policy
Service SAS with ad hoc SAS

questions.explanation:
A service SAS can grant permissions to a specific Azure Storage queue. Binding it to a stored access policy on that queue permits access to be revoked or changed centrally by modifying or deleting the policy, without regenerating storage account keys. Stored access policies apply to service-level SAS tokens and are supported for queues.

**Learn more:** [Define a stored access policy - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/define-stored-access-policy) · [Create a service SAS - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-service-sas)

You are building a microservices-based application that uses Azure Container Apps. The application includes several containerized services that perform tasks such as processing orders, managing inventory, and generating reports. You deploy two microservices, named serviceA and serviceB, to support inventory management.  
  
You have the following requirements:  
  
- serviceA and serviceB must publish events to one Azure Event Hub by using the Event Hubs SDK.  
- serviceA must publish 1,000 events per second.  
- serviceB must publish 3,000 events per second.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
You need to support event publishing.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create four partitions. Update serviceA to use one partition and serviceB to use three partitions.
Enable and configure Azure Event Hubs Capture.
Create an Azure Event Hubs dedicated cluster. Configure the capacity units to one and the scaling units to two.
Create and configure an Azure Schema Registry in Event Hubs. Update serviceA and serviceB to validate message schemas.
Create four consumer groups. Update serviceA to use one consumer group and serviceB to use three consumer groups.

questions.explanation:
Partitions provide parallel publishing paths in an event hub. Allocating one partition to the 1,000-events-per-second publisher and three partitions to the 3,000-events-per-second publisher supplies four parallel publishing paths while avoiding the additional cost and unrelated functionality of a dedicated cluster, Capture, Schema Registry, or consumer groups. In Standard tier, the namespace must also have sufficient throughput units because throughput units control total ingress capacity; each provides up to 1,000 ingress events per second. [Microsoft Learn: Scaling with Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-scalability)

**Learn more:** [Scaling with Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-scalability) · [Compare Azure Event Hubs tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/compare-tiers)

questions.question:
You have 100 Azure virtual machines (VMs) for which the system-assigned managed identity is enabled.  
  
You need to determine the object ID attribute value for each identity.  
  
Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
For a VM with a system-assigned managed identity, the managed identity's object ID is the resource identity `PrincipalId`. `Get-AzResource` retrieves the VM resource and exposes this value through `Identity.PrincipalId`.\
\
**Learn more:** [Assign a managed identity to an app role using PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/id-id/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/assign-app-role-managed-identity-powershell) · [Get-AzResource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.resources/get-azresource?view=azps-15.6.0&viewFallbackFrom=azps-14.5.0)

questions.question:
You have 100 Azure virtual machines (VMs) for which the system-assigned managed identity is enabled.  
  
You need to determine the object ID attribute value for each identity.  
  
Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Container Apps custom scaling rule uses the KEDA scaler `type` to identify the Event Hubs scaler and `metadata` to provide the scaler’s required Event Hubs settings and scaling threshold. Microsoft’s Container Apps scaling documentation maps these KEDA trigger fields to the custom rule’s `type` and `metadata` properties.

**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a microservices-based application that uses Azure Container Apps. The application includes several containerized services that perform tasks such as processing orders, managing inventory, and generating reports. You deploy a new revision of the processing orders app.  
  
Processing orders must be triggered by a web request and must always be available in response to incoming web requests.  
  
You need to verify that the replica is ready to handle incoming requests.  
  
What should you implement?
questions.explanation:
An HTTP readiness probe checks whether a replica is ready to receive incoming requests through an HTTP endpoint. Azure Container Apps uses readiness status to determine whether a revision can receive traffic, whereas startup and liveness probes serve different health-check purposes.

**Learn more:** [Health probes in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/health-probes)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You administer an Azure App Service web app named App1 and its associated Azure Application Insights resource, AppInsights1.  
  
You need alerts for any abnormal increase in the rate of failed HTTP requests directed at App1.  
  
You must implement push notifications.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures AppInsights1.
From the Azure portal, modify a smart detection rule of AppInsights1.
Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures the ProactiveDetectionConfigs child resource of AppInsights1.
From the Azure portal, modify an action group of Azure Monitor.

questions.explanation:
Application Insights Failure Anomalies detects abnormal increases in failed HTTP request rates. Azure Monitor action groups define alert notification channels and support Azure app push notifications, so the action group associated with the alert must be modified to add the push-notification receiver.

**Learn more:** [Smart Detection of Failure Anomalies in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/proactive-failure-diagnostics) · [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You build a web application that sells access to last-minute vacancies at child camps that operate on weekends. The application uses Azure Application Insights for all monitoring and alerting.  
  
The application must notify operators when a technical problem prevents camp sales.  
  
You need to create an alert that detects technical problems.  
  
Which alert type should you use?

options.text: Metric alert using multiple time series
Log alert using multiple time series

questions.explanation:
A metric alert with dynamic thresholds is suited to a sales metric whose normal behavior follows a weekend pattern. Dynamic thresholds learn historical metric behavior, including hourly, daily, and weekly patterns, and identify anomalous deviations such as an unexpected drop in sales that can indicate a technical failure. Multiple time series is intended for separately monitoring multiple dimension or resource series, which is not required here.

**Learn more:** [Alert rules with dynamic thresholds overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-dynamic-thresholds) · [Create Azure Monitor metric alert rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-create-metric-alert-rule)

questions.question:
You are a developer at your company.  
  
You need to modify the workflows for an existing Logic App.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Logic Apps Designer is the visual authoring interface for opening an existing workflow and editing its steps. Microsoft Learn states that the designer opens an existing workflow so you can edit the steps; Code view is specifically for editing the JSON workflow definition.\
\
**Learn more:** [Navigate the Standard Workflow Designer - Azure Logic Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/logic-apps/designer-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a solution that enables smart refrigerators to send temperature data to a central location.  
  
The solution must receive and retain messages until they can be processed. You create an Azure Service Bus instance by specifying a name, pricing tier, subscription, resource group, and location.  
  
You need to finish the configuration.  
  
Which Azure CLI or PowerShell command should you run?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Service Bus queue provides durable message storage so producers can send messages and consumers can process them later. Creating a queue in the existing Service Bus namespace completes the required messaging configuration.

**Learn more:** [New-AzServiceBusQueue (Az.ServiceBus)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.servicebus/new-azservicebusqueue?view=azps-15.3.0) · [Use the Azure CLI to create a Service Bus queue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-quickstart-cli)

options.text: Close the database connection and immediately report an error.
Disable connection pooling and configure a second Azure Database for MySQL instance.
Wait five seconds before repeating the connection attempt to the database.
Set a maximum number of connection attempts to 10 and report an error on subsequent connections.
Increase connection repeat attempts exponentially up to 120 seconds.

questions.explanation:
Transient Azure Database for MySQL connectivity failures should use retry logic that waits before the initial retry, increases retry delays exponentially when failures persist, and limits the number of retries before treating the operation as failed. This prevents immediate repeated requests during recovery while ensuring the application does not retry indefinitely.

**Learn more:** [Architecture Best Practices for Azure Database for MySQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/service-guides/azure-database-for-mysql) · [Transient Fault Handling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/best-practices/transient-faults)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Queue Storage account containing a queue named `queue1`.  
  
You plan to use the Azure SDK for .NET to develop a solution that uses `queue1`.  
  
You need to write C# code that returns an approximate count of the messages in `queue1`. The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
Which method should you use in your code?

options.text: GetProperties method of the QueueClient class
GetProperties method of the QueueServiceClient class
PeekMessages method of the QueueClient class
GetStatistics method of the QueueServiceClient class

questions.explanation:
`QueueClient.GetProperties` retrieves the properties of a specific queue, and the returned `QueueProperties.ApproximateMessagesCount` value provides the queue's approximate message count. This is the direct SDK operation for obtaining the estimate without retrieving messages.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Azure Queue Storage client library for .NET](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/queues/storage-quickstart-queues-dotnet) · [QueueClient.GetProperties Method (Azure.Storage.Queues)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/azure.storage.queues.queueclient.getproperties?view=azure-dotnet)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Basic gateway credentials for the HTTP(S) endpoint.  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure API Management can authenticate to a backend HTTP(S) API by using Basic credentials. The configured username and password are sent to the backend in the HTTP Authorization header, which provides back-end authentication for the API service.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure API Management policy reference - authentication-basic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/authentication-basic-policy) · [Authentication and authorization to APIs in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/authentication-authorization-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure Client cert gateway credentials for the HTTP(S) endpoint.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure API Management supports client-certificate authentication from the gateway to a backend HTTP(S) service. Client certificate gateway credentials configure the certificate that API Management presents to the backend, satisfying the requirement for backend authentication.\
\
**Learn more:** [Secure backend services by using client certificate authentication in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-howto-mutual-certificates)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure **Client cert** gateway credentials for the Azure resource.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure API Management supports mutual TLS authentication to a backend service by configuring a client certificate in the API’s Gateway credentials. Azure App Service can be configured for client-certificate authentication, so this provides backend authentication for the RESTful API.\
\
**Learn more:** [Secure backend services by using client certificate authentication in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-howto-mutual-certificates)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Basic gateway credentials for the Azure resource.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Basic gateway credentials send a username and password to a backend using HTTP Basic authentication; they do not configure Azure App Service backend authentication for the Azure resource. API Management supports configuring a client certificate as gateway authentication for a backend service, which is the applicable backend-authentication mechanism here.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authenticate with Basic — Azure API Management policy reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/authentication-basic-policy) · [Secure backend services by using client certificate authentication in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-howto-mutual-certificates)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a new Azure subscription. You are developing an internal employee website for viewing sensitive data. The website uses Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) for authentication.  
  
You need to implement multifactor authentication for the website.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure the website to use Azure AD B2C.
In Azure AD, create a new conditional access policy.
In Azure AD, enable application proxy.
In Azure AD conditional access, enable the baseline policy.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can require multifactor authentication when users access a selected application. Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licensing (formerly Azure AD Premium), so the required actions are to upgrade to Azure AD Premium and create a Conditional Access policy that requires MFA.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra licensing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/licensing) · [Verify mandatory MFA setup for Microsoft Entra users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-mandatory-multifactor-authentication)

You are developing a website that uses Azure Blob storage for data storage. You configure the Azure Blob storage lifecycle to move all blobs to the archive tier after 30 days.  
  
Customers have requested a service-level agreement (SLA) for viewing data more than 30 days old.  
  
You need to document the minimum SLA for data recovery.  
  
Which SLA should you use?
questions.explanation:
Blobs in the archive tier are offline and must be rehydrated to an online tier before they can be accessed. Standard-priority archive rehydration can take up to 15 hours, so the applicable recovery SLA is one to 15 hours.

**Learn more:** [Rehydrate an archived blob to an online tier - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/archive-rehydrate-to-online-tier) · [Access tiers for blob data - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/access-tiers-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a Java application that will be deployed in Azure. The application stores sensitive data in Azure Cosmos DB.  
  
You need to configure Always Encrypted so that the sensitive data is encrypted within the application.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a new container to include an encryption policy with the JSON properties to be encrypted.
Create a customer-managed key (CMK) and store the key in a new Azure Key Vault instance.
Create a data encryption key (DEK) by using the Azure Cosmos DB SDK and store the key in Azure Cosmos DB.
Create an Azure AD managed identity and assign the identity to a new Azure Key Vault instance.

questions.explanation:
Always Encrypted encrypts data with DEKs that are created client-side and stored in Azure Cosmos DB only after they are wrapped by a CMK. The CMK must be created in Azure Key Vault first; its key identifier is required when creating the DEK. The encryption policy is then specified when the container is created.

**Learn more:** [Use client-side encryption with Always Encrypted for Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-always-encrypted)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must authenticate a user to the corporate website as shown in the architectural diagram.  
  
Which two values should be used? Each correct answer provides part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
An ID token establishes a user's identity only after its signature has been validated and its claims have been verified. Signature validation confirms the token was issued by the trusted identity provider, while claim validation confirms properties such as the intended audience and issuer. Microsoft Entra ID documents that applications validating ID tokens should validate both the token signature and applicable claims.

**Learn more:** [OpenID Connect (OIDC) on the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc) · [ID token claims reference - Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/id-token-claims-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop a web application that provides access to legal documents stored in Azure Blob Storage using version-level immutability policies. The documents are protected by both time-based policies and legal-hold policies. Every time-based retention policy has the `AllowProtectedAppendWrites` property enabled.  
  
You must prevent users from attempting operations that would fail only if a legal hold is active and all other policies have expired.  
  
You need to meet the requirement.  
  
Which two operations should you prevent? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
With version-level immutability, overwriting a blob creates a new version, so an existing version’s legal hold does not block the overwrite. New blobs can also be created. `AllowProtectedAppendWrites` permits appending while a time-based retention policy is active; after that policy expires, an active legal hold prevents modifying the held document, including adding data. A legal hold also prevents deletion until it is explicitly cleared.

**Learn more:** [Version-level WORM policies for immutable blob data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-version-level-worm-policies) · [Store business-critical blob data with immutable storage in a WORM state](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-storage-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to troubleshoot the order workflow.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Power Automate trigger history indicates whether an event was received and the trigger fired, while run history shows the status and detailed errors of each workflow execution. Together, they distinguish a trigger problem from a failure in a later action of the workflow.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot common issues with Power Automate triggers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-automate/flow-run-issues/triggers-troubleshoot) · [Missing runs or triggers history for a flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-automate/flow-run-issues/missing-runs-or-triggers-history-for-a-flow)

questions.question:
You need to make sure that every message from Azure Event Grid is processed.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation: An Azure Service Bus queue provides durable, asynchronous messaging: Event Grid can deliver events to the queue, and consumers process and complete each message from that buffer. This decouples event delivery from processing and supports reliable handling when consumers are temporarily unavailable.

questions.question:
You must resolve an issue with notification latency.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Ensure that the Azure Function is using an App Service plan.
Ensure that the Azure Function is set to use a consumption plan.

questions.explanation:
On a dedicated App Service plan, an Azure Functions runtime can go idle after a period of inactivity. Enabling **Always On** keeps it running and prevents the associated startup latency. The Always On setting is available only when the function uses an App Service plan; Consumption-plan apps are activated automatically by the platform.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Functions dedicated hosting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/dedicated-plan#always-on)

Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

questions.explanation:
Active Directory integrated authentication uses Integrated Windows Authentication with the developer’s existing on-premises Active Directory credentials, provided the on-premises directory is joined to Microsoft Entra ID. You need to audit sales transactions from retail stores.  
  
Which two possible methods can achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Update the retail store location data upload process to include blob index tags. Create an Azure Function to process the blob index tags and filter by store location.
Process the change feed logs of the Azure Blob storage account by using an Azure Function. Specify a time range for the change feed data.
Enable blob versioning for the storage account. Use an Azure Function to process a list of the blob versions per day.
Process an Azure Storage blob inventory report by using an Azure Function. Create rule filters on the blob inventory report.
Subscribe to blob storage events by using an Azure Function and Azure Event Grid. Filter the events by store location.

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage change feed provides durable, immutable transaction logs for blob and blob-metadata changes and supports consuming the changes for selected time ranges. Azure Storage blob inventory creates scheduled, filterable reports of blobs and their properties, which can be processed to audit storage contents.

**Learn more:** [Change feed in Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-change-feed) · [Azure Storage blob inventory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/blob-inventory)

questions.explanation:
The `oid` claim is the immutable object identifier for the user account. It uniquely identifies the user across applications using the Microsoft identity platform.\

Solution: Update the app with a method named `statuscheck` that runs the scripts. Update the app settings for the app. Configure `WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_PATH` and `WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_STATUSES` with a path to the new method and appropriate response codes.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
`WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_PATH` configures the endpoint that Azure App Service pings to warm the target deployment slot during a swap. `WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_STATUSES` defines the HTTP status codes that allow the warm-up and swap to continue; other responses stop the operation. An endpoint that runs the required scripts and returns an accepted status code ensures those actions complete before the swap proceeds.\
\
**Learn more:** [Environment variables and app settings in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/reference-app-settings)

questions.question:
Solution: Turn on auto swap for the Testing slot. Deploy the app to the Testing slot.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Auto swap warms the source slot before swapping, but enabling it does not configure custom initialization actions. For Windows-hosted Azure App Service apps, the `applicationInitialization` element in `Web.config` specifies custom warm-up actions, and App Service waits for that warm-up to finish before swapping with the target slot.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up staging environments in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-staging-slots)

questions.question:
Solution: Turn off auto swap. Update the app with a method called `statuscheck` that runs the scripts. Turn auto swap back on, and deploy the app to the Production slot.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
App Service requires a configured warm-up path or application-initialization configuration to call an endpoint before a slot swap. Adding a `statuscheck` method alone does not cause App Service to invoke it; `WEBSITE_SWAP_WARMUP_PING_PATH` must be set to a path such as `/statuscheck`, or equivalent application initialization must be configured.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up staging environments in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-staging-slots) · [Environment variables and app settings reference for Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/reference-app-settings)

questions.question:

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service supports custom pre-swap warm-up through the `applicationInitialization` element in `Web.config`. The platform runs the specified initialization actions and waits for the custom warm-up to finish before completing the slot swap.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up staging environments in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-staging-slots)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing several APIs hosted in Azure API Management (APIM).  
  
You must inspect API request processing in APIM, including requests made to APIM by using a REST client. The request inspection must include the following information:  
  
- Requests APIM sent to the API backend and the response that it received  
- Policies applied to the response before it is returned to the caller  
- Errors that occurred while processing the request and the policies applied to those errors  
- The original request APIM received from the caller and the policies applied to the request  
  
You need to inspect the APIs.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Enable the Allow tracing setting for the subscription used to inspect the API.
Add the Ocp-Apim-Trace header value to the API call whit a value set to true.
Add the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header value to the key for a subscription that allows access to the API.
Create and configure a custom policy. Apply the policy to the inbound policy section with a global scope.
Create and configure a custom policy. Apply the policy to the outbound policy section with an API scope.

questions.explanation:
In the legacy subscription-based APIM tracing model, complete request traces are enabled by allowing tracing on the subscription, sending `Ocp-Apim-Trace: true`, and including an `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` for a subscription that can access the API. The built-in trace records inbound, backend, outbound, and error processing, including policy execution; custom inbound or outbound policies are not required. Current APIM documentation notes that this legacy subscription/header mechanism is no longer supported and has been replaced by time-limited API-level trace tokens.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Debug APIs in Azure API Management using request tracing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-howto-api-inspector) · [Azure API Management policy reference - trace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/trace-policy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to lower read latency for the retail store solution.  
  
What are two possible methods to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a new composite index for the store location data queries in Azure Cosmos DB. Modify the queries to support parameterized SQL and update the Azure Function app to call the new queries.
Provision an Azure Cosmos DB dedicated gateway. Update the Azure Function app connection string to use the new dedicated gateway endpoint.
Configure Azure Cosmos DB consistency to session consistency. Cache session tokens in a new Azure Redis cache instance after every write. Update reads to use the session token stored in Azure Redis.
Provision an Azure Cosmos DB dedicated gateway. Update blob storage to use the new dedicated gateway endpoint.
Configure Azure Cosmos DB consistency to strong consistency. Increase the RUs for the container supporting store location data.

questions.explanation:
Composite indexes improve the efficiency of applicable Azure Cosmos DB queries, including queries with multiple filters or filtering and sorting, which can reduce query execution cost and latency. A dedicated gateway supplies a dedicated endpoint and integrated cache; requests routed through it have lower, more predictable latency than those using the standard gateway, and cache hits are served from memory.

**Learn more:** [Azure Cosmos DB dedicated gateway overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/dedicated-gateway) · [Azure Cosmos DB indexing policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/index-policy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage an Azure App Service web app named App1 and its associated Azure Application Insights resource, AppInsights1.  
  
You need alerts for any abnormal increase in the rate of failed HTTP requests directed to App1.  
  
You must implement push notifications.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Azure portal, create a service health alert of Azure Monitor.
From the Azure portal, modify a smart detection rule of AppInsights1.
Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures AppInsights1.
From the Azure portal, modify an action group of Azure Monitor.

questions.explanation:
Application Insights Smart Detection Failure Anomalies detects unusual increases in failed HTTP request rates. Azure Monitor action groups define alert notification delivery and support Azure app push notifications, so the action group associated with the alert must be modified to include the push notification action.

**Learn more:** [Smart Detection of Failure Anomalies in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/proactive-failure-diagnostics) · [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to implement a solution that resolves the retail store location data issue.  
  
Which three Azure Blob features should you enable? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Blob point-in-time restore depends on blob versioning, blob soft delete, and change feed. Versioning maintains prior blob states, soft delete retains deleted blobs and versions for the configured retention period, and change feed records the blob changes needed to restore block blobs to an earlier point in time.

**Learn more:** [Data protection overview for Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/data-protection-overview) · [Change feed support in Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-change-feed)

## Background

Fourth Coffee is a global coffeehouse chain and coffee company recognized as one of the world’s most influential coffee brands. The company is known for its specialty coffee beverages, including a broad range of espresso-based drinks, teas, and other beverages. Fourth Coffee operates thousands of stores worldwide.

## Current environment

The company is building cloud-native applications hosted in Azure.

## Corporate website

The company hosts a public website at `http://www.fourthcoffee.com/`. The website is used to place orders and view and update inventory items.

## Inventory items

In addition to its core coffee offerings, Fourth Coffee recently expanded its menu to include inventory items such as lunch items, snacks, and merchandise. Corporate team members continuously update inventory. Users can customize items. Corporate team members configure inventory items and associated images on the website.

## Orders

Associates in the store serve customized beverages and items to customers. Orders are placed on the website for pickup.

The application components process data as follows:

1. Azure Traffic Manager routes a user order request to the corporate website hosted in Azure App Service.
2. Azure Content Delivery Network serves static images and content to the user.
3. The user signs in to the application through a Microsoft Entra ID for customers tenant.
4. Users search for items and place an order on the website as item images are pulled from Azure Blob Storage.
5. Item customizations are placed in an Azure Service Bus queue message.
6. Azure Functions processes item customizations and saves the customized items to Azure Cosmos DB.
7. The website saves order details to Azure SQL Database.
8. SQL Database query results are cached in Azure Cache for Redis to improve performance.

The application consists of the following Azure services:

![Scenario Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783877967549-ozbv20ex.png)

## Requirements

The application components must meet the following requirements:

- Azure Cosmos DB development must use a native API that receives the latest updates and stores data in a document format.
- Costs must be minimized for all Azure services.
- Developers must test Azure Blob Storage integrations locally before deployment to Azure. Testing must support the latest versions of the Azure Storage APIs.

### Corporate website

- User authentication and authorization must allow one-time passcode sign-in methods and social identity providers (Google or Facebook).
- Static web content must be stored closest to end users to reduce network latency.

### Inventory items

- Customized items read from Azure Cosmos DB must maximize throughput while ensuring data is accurate for the current user on the website.
- Processing of inventory item updates must automatically scale and enable updates across an entire Azure Cosmos DB container.
- Inventory items must be processed in the order they were placed in the queue.
- Inventory item images must be stored as JPEG files in their native format to include exchangeable image file format (data) stored with the blob data upon upload of the image file.
- The Inventory Items API must securely access the Azure Cosmos DB data.

### Orders

- Orders must receive inventory item changes automatically after inventory items are updated or saved.

## Issues

- Developers are storing the Azure Cosmos DB credentials in an insecure clear text manner within the Inventory Items API code.
- Production Azure Cache for Redis maintenance has negatively affected application performance.33:["$","div",null,{"className":"exam-content","children":[["$","$L3c",null,{"group":{"id":"3be912fc2668e5694f80c2b9415c97796eb5108677f64a0401159afaa761e8bb","type":"case_study","title":"Fourth Coffee Azure Commerce Modernization","content":"$3d"}}],"$L3e","$L3f"]}]
You need to mitigate the Azure Cache for Redis issue.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Test application code by rebooting all nodes in the test environment.
Configure client connections to retry commands with exponential backoff.
Modify the maxmemory policy to evict the least frequently used keys out of all keys.
Increase the maxmemory-reserved and maxfragmentationmemory-reserved values.
Test application code by purging the cache in the test environment.

questions.explanation:
Maintenance-related failovers can add replication load and cause latency or timeouts. Client retry logic with exponential backoff handles transient connection and command failures. Increasing `maxmemory-reserved` and `maxfragmentationmemory-reserved` reserves memory for non-cache operations and fragmentation, helping the cache remain responsive under failover and maintenance load.

**Learn more:** [Failover and patching - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-failover) · [Best practices for memory management - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-best-practices-memory-management)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to deliver static content from the corporate website.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Store all static content in Azure Blob Storage. Enable Azure Content Delivery Network for the storage account.
Configure App Service networking to create a Content Delivery Network profile and endpoint.
Configure the Azure App Service Local Cache feature and set the app setting WEBSITE_LOCAL_CACHE_SIZEINMB value.
Create a nested Azure Traffic Manager profile. Configure the parent profile to the performance traffic routing method and the child profile to the priority traffic routing method.
Update the Azure Traffic Manager routing method to priority.

questions.explanation:
Azure Content Delivery Network caches static web content at globally distributed edge locations. A CDN endpoint can use either Azure Blob Storage or an Azure App Service web app as its origin, so storing the static assets in Blob Storage and enabling CDN, or creating a CDN profile and endpoint for the App Service site, both meet the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Azure CDN REST API overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/cdn/) · [Create an Azure CDN origin](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/cdn/origins/create?view=rest-cdn-2025-04-15)
