You need to implement processing for enqueued inventory items.  
  
Which message value should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus sessions provide FIFO processing for related messages. Assigning the same session identifier to the inventory-item messages causes Service Bus to process that session’s messages in order; a sequence number alone does not guarantee processing order when multiple consumers are used.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus message sessions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/message-sessions)

questions.explanation:
Cosmos DB data can be secured either with Microsoft Entra identity + RBAC (no keys) or by protecting the keys in Key Vault. Option A uses a user-assigned managed identity granted a Cosmos DB SQL role definition and DefaultAzureCredential - a keyless, complete approach. Option E stores the Cosmos DB URI and primary key as Key Vault secrets and references them from function app settings via a system-assigned managed identity with secret-read access - complete. Option D uses a custom Entra role scoped to Key Vault to let the function app read the values - complete. Option B is incorrect because after creating a SQL role it then 'programmatically accesses the Cosmos DB keys,' contradicting the role-based approach, and option C bases access on certificate authentication against a custom role assigned to the account, which is not a valid keyless data-plane pattern.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure API Management (APIM) Standard tier instance named APIM1 that uses a managed gateway.  
  
You plan to use APIM1 to publish an API named API1 that uses a backend database supporting only a limited number of requests per minute. You also require a policy for API1 that minimizes the possibility that requests to the backend database from each individual IP address you specify exceed the supported limit.  
  
You need to identify a policy for API1 that meets the requirements.  
  
Which policy should you use?
questions.explanation:
The `rate-limit-by-key` policy limits the call rate for each counter key during a specified renewal period. Setting its counter key to the caller's IP address applies the per-minute limit independently to each IP address, helping protect a backend database with a per-minute request constraint.

**Learn more:** [Azure API Management policy reference - rate-limit-by-key](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/rate-limit-by-key-policy) · [Advanced request throttling with Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-sample-flexible-throttling)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application that stores business-critical data in Azure Blob storage.  
  
The application must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Data must not be changed or deleted for a user-specified interval.  
- Data must be safeguarded against overwrites and deletions.  
- Data must be written once and readable many times.  
  
You need to protect the data in the Azure Blob storage account.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure a time-based retention policy for the storage account.
Enable the blob change feed for the storage account.
Enable version-level immutability support for the storage account.
Enable point-in-time restore for containers in the storage account.

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob immutable storage supports a write-once, read-many (WORM) state. A time-based retention policy prevents protected blob data from being modified or deleted for the configured retention interval. Version-level immutability support must be enabled before a default version-level time-based retention policy can be configured for a storage account.

**Learn more:** [Configure immutability policies for blob versions - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-policy-configure-version-scope) · [Version-level WORM policies for immutable blob data - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-version-level-worm-policies)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop a Python image-rendering application that uses GPU resources to optimize rendering operations. You deploy the application to an Azure Container Instances (ACI) Linux container.  
  
The application needs a secret value supplied when the container starts. The value must be accessible only from inside the container.  
  
You need to provide the secret value.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer is a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create an environment variable Set the secureValue property to the secret value.
Add the secret value to the container image. Use a managed identity.
Add the secret value to the application code Set the container startup command.
Add the secret value to an Azure Blob storage account. Generate a SAS token.
Mount a secret volume containing the secret value in a secrets file.

questions.explanation:
Azure Container Instances supports secure environment variables by using the `secureValue` property; the value is not displayed in container properties and can be accessed only within the container. ACI Linux containers also support read-only secret volumes, which provide secrets as files mounted inside the container.

**Learn more:** [Set environment variables in container instances](https://learn.microsoft.com/lb-lu/azure/container-instances/container-instances-environment-variables) · [Mount a secret volume in Azure Container Instances](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-volume-secret)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to resolve the error in the `RequestUserApproval` Function app.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Update line RA13 to use the async keyword and return an HttpRequest object value.
Configure the Function app to use an App Service hosting plan. Enable the Always On setting of the hosting plan.
Update the function to be stateful by using Durable Functions to process the request payload.

questions.explanation:
Approval workflows require a stateful process that can pause for a human response, receive that response as an external event, and optionally handle a timeout. Durable Functions provide durable orchestration state and the human-interaction pattern for this purpose; a standard HTTP-triggered function cannot remain awaiting an approval response indefinitely.

**Learn more:** [Human interaction pattern in Durable Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/durable-task/common/durable-task-human-interaction) · [Azure Functions HTTP trigger](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-http-webhook-trigger)

Azure Web PubSub validates each configured upstream webhook using CloudEvents abuse protection. The validation request contains the `WebHook-Request-Origin` header, and the webhook must recognize it and respond with an appropriate `WebHook-Allowed-Origin` value. A CDN in front of the Azure Function must therefore allow `WebHook-Request-Origin` to pass through.

**Learn more:** [Azure Web PubSub troubleshooting guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-web-pubsub/howto-troubleshoot-common-issues) · [Azure Web PubSub service internals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-web-pubsub/concept-service-internals)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates multiple web and mobile applications. Each application uses custom, in-house identity providers and social identity providers.  
  
You need to implement single sign-on (SSO) across all the applications.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Azure Active Directory B2C (Azure AD B2C) with custom policies.
Use Azure Active Directory B2B (Azure AD B2B) and enable external collaboration.
Use Azure Active Directory B2C (Azure AD B2C) with user flows.
Use Azure Active Directory B2B (Azure AD B2B).

questions.explanation:
Azure AD B2C supports federation with social and external identity providers for customer-facing applications. Its custom policies are fully configurable and can orchestrate trust with identity providers through protocols such as OpenID Connect, OAuth, and SAML, making them appropriate for a shared SSO experience that includes custom in-house providers. Azure AD B2B external collaboration is designed to grant guest users access to organizational resources rather than to provide consumer identity journeys.

**Learn more:** [Azure Active Directory B2C custom policy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-b2c/custom-policy-overview) · [Add an identity provider to your Azure AD B2C tenant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-b2c/add-identity-provider)

Schedule-based autoscale for Azure App Service is supported at the Standard tier and above. Premium V2 is therefore not the lowest-cost tier that provides the required capability, so scaling to Premium V2 does not minimize cost.\

The Shared App Service tier uses shared compute and cannot scale out. Schedule-based autoscaling applies to the App Service plan and requires the Autoscale capability available in Standard and higher tiers; therefore, a Shared-tier plan cannot meet the schedule-based autoscaling requirement, even though it costs less. [Azure App Service Plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plans)\

\
**Learn more:** [How to Enable Automatic Scaling - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/manage-automatic-scaling) · [Plan and Manage Costs for App Service - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-manage-costs)

/>","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an Azure Function that connects to an Azure SQL Database instance. The function is triggered by an Azure Storage queue.  
  
You receive reports of numerous `System.InvalidOperationExceptions` with the following message:  
  
`Timeout expired. The timeout period elapsed prior to obtaining a connection from the pool. This may have occurred because all pooled connections were in use and max pool size was reached.`  
  
You need to prevent this exception. What should you do?

options.text: In the host.json file, decrease the value of the batchSize option
Convert the trigger to Azure Event Hub
Convert the Azure Function to the Premium plan
In the function.json file, change the value of the type option to queueScaling

questions.explanation:
An Azure Storage queue trigger retrieves and processes queue messages concurrently. The `batchSize` setting in `host.json` controls the number of messages processed in parallel, so decreasing it reduces concurrent Azure Function invocations and their simultaneous Azure SQL Database connection usage. This avoids exhausting the SQL connection pool.

**Learn more:** [Azure Queue storage trigger and bindings for Azure Functions overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-storage-queue)

questions.question:
Your company is developing an Azure-hosted Azure API.  
  
You need to implement authentication so that the Azure API can access other Azure resources. You have the following requirements:  
  
- All API calls must be authenticated.  
- API callers must not send credentials to the API.  
  
Which authentication mechanism should you use?
questions.explanation:
Managed identity provides an Azure-hosted workload with an automatically managed Microsoft Entra identity that it can use to obtain tokens for authorized access to Azure resources. Azure manages the underlying credentials, so callers do not need to send credentials to the API.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is managed identities for Azure resources?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview)

questions.question:
Your company is developing an Azure-hosted Azure API.  
  
You need to implement authentication so that the Azure API can access other Azure resources. You have the following requirements:  
  
- All API calls must be authenticated.  
- API callers must not send credentials to the API.  
  
Which authentication mechanism should you use?

options.text: Create a partition for each retailer.
Define a namespace for each retailer.

questions.explanation:
Azure Event Hubs publisher policies provide granular control for many independent publishers. Each publisher uses a unique identifier, and the publisher name must match the SAS token used for authentication; consequently, assigning each retailer its identifier as its publisher identity restricts it to publishing its own sales. Partitions organize event streams and namespaces provide broader resource scoping, neither of which enforces publisher-specific sending rights.

**Learn more:** [Event Hubs features and terminology - Azure Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-features) · [Publisher policy operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/eventhub/publisher-policy-operations)

questions.question:
You develop a Web App that uses a D1 App Service plan.  
  
You observe that page-load times rise during peak-traffic periods.  
  
You want to implement automatic scaling when CPU load exceeds 80 percent. Your solution must minimize costs.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Enable autoscaling on the Web App.
Switch to the Premium App Service tier plan.
Switch to the Standard App Service tier plan.
Switch to the Azure App Services consumption plan.

questions.explanation:
The Shared (D1) tier cannot scale out. Autoscaling is available in the Standard tier and higher, so moving the App Service plan to Standard provides the required CPU-based autoscaling capability at lower cost than Premium.\
\
**Learn more:** [Plan and manage costs for Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-manage-costs) · [Azure App Service plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plans)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage an Azure subscription containing 100 Azure App Service web apps. Each web app is linked to a separate Application Insights instance.  
  
You plan to remove Classic availability tests from every Application Insights instance where this functionality is configured.  
  
You have the following PowerShell statement:  
  
```powershell  
Get-AzApplicationInsightsWebTest | Where-Object \{ $condition \}  
```  
  
You need to set the value of the `$condition` variable.  
  
Which value should you use?
questions.explanation:
Classic URL-ping availability tests have `WebTestKind` set to `ping`. `Get-AzApplicationInsightsWebTest` exposes this property for filtering, whereas `Type` represents the Azure resource type; `standard` denotes a Standard test rather than a Classic ping test.

**Learn more:** [Get-AzApplicationInsightsWebTest (Az.ApplicationInsights)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.applicationinsights/get-azapplicationinsightswebtest?view=azps-16.0.0) · [Web Tests - Get - REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/application-insights/web-tests/get?view=rest-application-insights-2022-06-15)

questions.question:
You are developing a road-tollway tracking application that sends tracking events by using Azure Event Hubs in the Premium tier.  
  
Each road must be assigned a unique throttling policy.  
  
You need to configure the event hub to support per-road throttling.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use a unique consumer group for each road.
Ensure each road stores events in a different partition.
Ensure each road has a unique connection string.
Use a unique application group for each road.

questions.explanation:
Azure Event Hubs application groups support throttling policies and are available in the Premium tier. Assigning each road to its own application group permits a distinct throttling policy for that road.\
\
**Learn more:** [Resource governance with application groups - Azure Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/resource-governance-overview)

questions.question:
Your company is developing an API in Azure.  
  
You must implement authentication for the Azure API and meet the following requirements:  
  
- All API calls must be secure.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783790054162-qxdo0k9v.png)  
  
- API callers must not send credentials to the API.  
  
Which authentication mechanism should be used?
questions.explanation:
Managed identities let Azure-hosted workloads obtain Microsoft Entra ID tokens without storing, managing, or sending credentials to the target API. The API can validate the token and authorize the managed identity, providing authenticated secure access without caller-supplied secrets or certificates.\
\
**Learn more:** [Managed identities for Azure resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview)

You are developing an Azure Cosmos DB solution using the Azure Cosmos DB SQL API. The data contains millions of documents, and each document can contain hundreds of properties.  
  
The document properties do not have distinct values suitable for partitioning. Azure Cosmos DB must scale individual containers in the database to satisfy the application's performance requirements by distributing the workload evenly across all partitions over time.  
  
You need to choose a partition key.  
  
Which two partition keys can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a single property value that does not appear frequently in the documents
a value containing the collection name
a single property value that appears frequently in the documents
a concatenation of multiple property values with a random suffix appended
a hash suffix appended to a property value

questions.explanation:
Synthetic partition keys provide adequate cardinality and distribution when no single property is sufficiently distinct. Concatenating multiple property values with a random suffix spreads writes across partition-key values, and appending a calculated hash suffix similarly distributes workload while allowing the suffix to be reproduced for targeted reads.

**Learn more:** [Create a synthetic partition key - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/synthetic-partition-keys) · [Partitioning and horizontal scaling - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/partitioning)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a web app protected by Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF). All traffic to the web app passes through an Azure Application Gateway instance that is shared by multiple web apps. The web app address is `contoso.azurewebsites.net`.  
  
All traffic must be protected with SSL. The Azure Application Gateway instance is shared by multiple web apps.  
  
You need to configure Azure Application Gateway for the web app.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: In the Azure Application Gateway's HTTP setting, enable the Use for App service setting.
Convert the web app to run in an Azure App service environment (ASE).
Add an authentication certificate for contoso.azurewebsites.net to the Azure Application Gateway.
In the Azure Application Gateway's HTTP setting, set the value of the Override backend path option to contoso22.azurewebsites.net.

questions.explanation:
For an App Service backend using its default `azurewebsites.net` domain, the Application Gateway HTTP setting must use the App Service-specific setting so the backend request uses the appropriate App Service host name. End-to-end HTTPS also requires Application Gateway to authenticate and trust the backend server certificate for `contoso.azurewebsites.net`.

**Learn more:** [Configure App Service with Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/configure-web-app)

You are developing a microservice that will run on Azure Container Apps for a company. External HTTP ingress traffic is enabled.  
  
The company requires that updates to the microservice do not cause downtime.  
  
You need to deploy an update to the microservice.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use multiple environments for each container.
Use a private container registry and single image for all containers.
Use a single environment for all containers.

questions.explanation:
In Azure Container Apps single revision mode, the existing revision continues to receive 100% of ingress traffic until the new revision is successfully provisioned, scaled, and passes its startup and readiness probes. This provides zero-downtime deployment; if the update fails, traffic remains on the existing revision.

**Learn more:** [Update and deploy changes in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/revisions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an Azure Function App that processes images uploaded to an Azure Blob container.  
  
Images must be processed as soon as possible after they are uploaded, and the solution must minimize latency. You create code that processes images when the Function App is triggered.  
  
You need to configure the Function App.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use an App Service plan. Configure the Function App to use an Azure Blob Storage input trigger.
Use a Consumption plan. Configure the Function App to use an Azure Blob Storage trigger.
Use a Consumption plan. Configure the Function App to use a Timer trigger.
Use an App Service plan. Configure the Function App to use an Azure Blob Storage trigger.
Use a Consumption plan. Configure the Function App to use an Azure Blob Storage input trigger.

questions.explanation:
A Blob Storage trigger runs a function in response to a new or updated blob, whereas a Blob Storage input binding only supplies blob data to a function that has already been invoked. Blob-trigger processing on a Consumption plan can be delayed when the app has gone idle. An App Service plan can use Always On to avoid that idle delay, making it the appropriate listed plan for low-latency image processing.

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob storage trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-storage-blob-trigger)

questions.question:
You are developing an app that will use CosmosDB for data storage. The app will process batches of relational data.  
  
You need to choose an API for the app.  
  
Which API should you use?

Azure Cosmos DB SQL API supports SQL-like queries and relational query operators over JSON documents, making it the appropriate API for processing relational data batches.\
\
**Learn more:** [Query Documents - Azure Cosmos DB REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/cosmos-db/query-documents)

You have a workspace-based Azure Application Insights resource named Insights1 and an Azure App Service web app named App1. Insights1 collects telemetry produced by App1.  
  
You plan to evaluate the alerting capability of the availability testing enabled for App1 by taking it offline for 50 minutes.  
  
You create a standard availability test for App1, configure its frequency as 15 minutes, and set its alert status to Enabled.  
  
You need to determine how many alerts to expect when App1 is offline for 50 minutes.  
  
How many alerts should you expect?
questions.explanation:
Application Insights availability alerts are state-based: one alert is generated when the endpoint is detected as unavailable, and no further alerts are generated at later evaluations while it remains unavailable. A 15-minute test frequency does not cause repeated alerts during the same 50-minute outage.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Hyper-V hosts, named Host1 and Host2. Host1 contains an Azure virtual machine named VM1 that was deployed using a custom Azure Resource Manager template.  
  
You need to move VM1 to Host2.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Update management blade, click Enable.
From the Overview blade, move VM1 to a different subscription.
From the Redeploy blade, click Redeploy.
From the Profile blade, modify the usage location.

questions.explanation:
Redeploying an Azure virtual machine shuts it down, moves it to a new Azure infrastructure node, and powers it back on while retaining its configuration and associated resources. The Redeploy operation performs the required host move.

**Learn more:** [Redeploy Linux virtual machine to new Azure node](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-machines/linux/redeploy-to-new-node-linux) · [Virtual Machines - Redeploy REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/compute/virtual-machines/redeploy?view=rest-compute-2026-03-02)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop and deploy an Azure App Service web app. The app is deployed across multiple regions and uses Azure Traffic Manager. Application Insights is enabled for the app.  
  
You need to analyze the app uptime for each month.  
  
Which two solutions will achieve the goal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
To analyze monthly uptime you need availability data plus a way to query it over time. Application Insights availability (web/URL ping) tests (D) actively probe the app from multiple locations and record availability results, which is the standard mechanism for measuring uptime of a Traffic Manager-fronted, multi-region app. Azure Monitor Logs (A) stores those availabilityResults and lets you run KQL queries to aggregate uptime per month. Azure Monitor metrics (C) retains data for a limited window and is not suited to per-month historical analysis, and Application Insights alerts (B) only notify on conditions rather than analyze uptime, so each is an incomplete solution.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application that transfers data between on-premises file servers and Azure Blob storage. The application stores keys, secrets, and certificates in Azure Key Vault and uses the Azure Key Vault APIs.  
  
You need to configure the application so that an accidentally deleted key vault or key vault object can be recovered for 90 days after deletion.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Run the az keyvault update --enable-soft-delete true --enable-purge-protection true CLI.
Implement virtual network service endpoints for Azure Key Vault.
Run the az keyvault update --enable-soft-delete false CLI.

questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault soft delete retains deleted vaults and vault objects for a recoverable retention period, which defaults to 90 days. Purge protection prevents permanent purging during that period. Enabling both features provides recovery protection for accidentally deleted vaults, keys, secrets, and certificates.

**Learn more:** [Azure Key Vault recovery management with soft delete and purge protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/key-vault-recovery) · [Azure CLI: az keyvault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/keyvault?view=azure-cli-latest)

You are building an ASP.NET Core Web API web service. The web service uses Azure Application Insights for all telemetry and dependency tracking. The web service reads from and writes to a database other than Microsoft SQL Server.  
  
You need to make sure dependency tracking functions for calls to the third-party database.  
  
Which two dependency telemetry properties should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
For custom dependency tracking across a remote boundary, the dependency telemetry `Id` serves as the parent identifier and `Context.Operation.Id` identifies the root operation. Propagating these correlation identifiers lets related telemetry be associated with the same end-to-end operation. Application Insights defines dependency `Id` as the unique dependency-call identifier used to correlate the call with its corresponding request.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights telemetry data model](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/data-model-complete) · [Dependency tracking in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/dependencies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a web application that analyzes user photos and returns metadata about the objects it identifies. Image analysis is very expensive in both time and compute resources. You plan to use Azure Redis Cache so that duplicate uploads do not require reprocessing.  
  
In the event of an Azure data-center outage, metadata loss must be minimized.  
  
You need to configure the Azure Redis cache instance.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure Azure Redis with AOF persistence.
Configure Azure Redis with RDB persistence.
Configure second storage account for persistence.
Set backup frequency to the minimum value.

questions.explanation:
AOF persistence saves every cache write operation to an append-only log and persists that log once per second, providing substantially lower potential data loss than scheduled RDB snapshots. For Premium Azure Cache for Redis, AOF persistence can be configured with a second storage account, allowing persisted AOF data to be distributed across the configured storage accounts.

**Learn more:** [Data persistence - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-how-to-premium-persistence)

options.text: Add the customer ID for the signed in user to the CorrelationContext in the web application
On the current SpanContext, set the TraceId to the customer ID for the signed in user
Set the header Ocp-Apim-Trace to the customer ID for the signed in user
Create a new SpanContext with the TraceFlags value set to the customer ID for the signed in user

questions.explanation:
CorrelationContext propagates application-defined name-value distributed-tracing properties with an operation, so placing the signed-in user's customer ID in it associates that value with telemetry and downstream HTTP operations. Trace IDs and trace flags are reserved tracing fields, not containers for business identifiers.

**Learn more:** [Add and modify OpenTelemetry in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/opentelemetry-add-modify?tabs=net) · [Application Insights JavaScript SDK configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/javascript-sdk-configuration)

questions.question:
You have 100 Azure virtual machines (VMs) with system-assigned managed identities enabled.  
  
You need to determine the value of the object ID attribute for each identity.  
  
Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
For a system-assigned managed identity, the managed identity service principal’s object ID is the resource identity’s `PrincipalId`. `Get-AzResource` retrieves the VM resource, allowing its `Identity.PrincipalId` value to be obtained.\
\
**Learn more:** [Assign an application role to a managed identity using PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/assign-app-role-managed-identity-powershell)

questions.question:
You have 100 Azure virtual machines (VMs) with system-assigned managed identities enabled.  
  
You need to determine the value of the object ID attribute for each identity.  
  
Which command should you use?

options.text: Create a collection sharded on username to store documents.
Configure Azure Cosmos DB to use the Gremlin API.
Create an unsharded collection to store documents.
Configure Azure Cosmos DB to use the MongoDB API.

questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB provides multi-document transactions with ACID semantics only within a single unsharded collection. Multi-document transactions are not supported in sharded collections, so the required configuration is an unsharded collection using the MongoDB API.

**Learn more:** [Use multi-document transactions in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/use-multi-document-transactions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Queue Storage queue named `queue1`.  
  
You plan to develop code to process messages in `queue1`.  
  
You need to implement a queue operation that sets the visibility-timeout value for individual messages in `queue1`.  
  
Which two operations can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Peek at a message in the queue.
Delete a message in the queue.
Add a message to the queue.
Update a message in the queue.
Receive a message from the queue.

questions.explanation:
The Receive/Get Messages operation accepts a `visibilitytimeout` parameter, which makes each retrieved message invisible to other consumers for the specified period. The Update Message operation explicitly changes the visibility timeout of an identified message, using its message ID and pop receipt.

**Learn more:** [Get Messages (REST API) - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/get-messages) · [Update Message (REST API) - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/update-message)

questions.question:
You need to make sure that the solution can satisfy the scaling requirements for Policy Service.  
  
Which Azure Application Insights data model should you use?
questions.explanation: Application Insights metrics store and aggregate numeric measurements over time, supporting monitoring and alerting for service load, performance, and capacity indicators that determine whether scaling requirements are being met.

questions.question:
Solution: Install the Docker client on the device and run the `docker run -it microsoft/azure-cli:0.10.17` command.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
An AKS manifest deployment requires `kubectl` configured with cluster credentials, typically obtained with `az aks get-credentials`, and deployment with `kubectl apply -f <manifest>`. Starting an Azure CLI container alone neither configures Kubernetes access nor applies the YAML manifest.\
\
**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Deploy an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster using Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/learn/quick-kubernetes-deploy-cli)

questions.question:
Solution: You install the Azure CLI on the device and run the `kubectl apply "f myapp.yaml` command.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation: A YAML manifest is deployed with kubectl by using the `-f` flag, such as `kubectl apply -f myapp.yaml`. The Azure CLI alone does not install kubectl, and the command shown does not use the valid manifest-file flag syntax.

questions.question:
Solution: Deploy and configure an Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and update the web applications.  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cache for Redis is the Azure service that supports shared ASP.NET session state with controlled concurrent access for multiple readers and a single writer, as well as cached HTML output/HTTP responses. Azure Database for PostgreSQL alone does not provide this session-state and output-caching mechanism.\
\
**Learn more:** [Caching guidance — Azure Architecture Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/best-practices/caching) · [What is Azure Cache for Redis?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: Turn on Application Request Routing (ARR).  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
ARR affinity provides sticky-session routing to the same App Service instance; it does not store or share session state or full HTTP responses. The required distributed state and response storage capabilities therefore are not met.\
\
**Learn more:** [ASP.NET Core SignalR production hosting and scaling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/signalr/scale?view=aspnetcore-9.0)

questions.question:
Solution: Deploy and configure Azure Cache for Redis, and update the web applications.  
  
Does the solution satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cache for Redis functions as a shared distributed session store and provides an ASP.NET output-cache provider for cached HTTP responses. ASP.NET session-state provider behavior supports exclusive session-item locking during writes, while read-only session access does not acquire that lock, enabling the required controlled concurrent access.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Cache for Redis?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-overview) · [ASP.NET Core output cache provider for Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/redis/aspnet-core-output-cache-provider)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You deploy an Azure App Service web app and create an app registration for it in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) and Twitter.  
  
The app must authenticate users, use SSL for all communications, and use Twitter as the identity provider.  
  
You need to validate the Azure AD request in the app code.  
  
What should you validate?
questions.explanation:
An ID token is a signed JWT, so validating its signature with the identity provider’s published signing keys verifies that the token was issued by the trusted provider and has not been altered. Token validation should also validate applicable claims, but the signature is the relevant validation among these choices.

**Learn more:** [Access tokens in the Microsoft identity platform — Validate tokens](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/access-tokens) · [OpenID Connect (OIDC) on the Microsoft identity platform — Validate the ID token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc)

You create an Azure subscription called Sub1. In Sub1, you create a custom Azure Event Grid topic named Topic1. You then create an Event Grid event subscription named EventSub1. EventSub1 uses Topic1 as its event source and a Web Hook as its endpoint.  
  
You plan to enable dead-lettering for EventSub1.  
  
You need to ensure that dead-lettering can be enabled for EventSub1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create an Azure Blob Storage container in Sub1.
Create an Azure Storage queue in Sub1.
Configure the retry policy of EventSub1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid dead-lettering stores undeliverable events in an Azure Blob Storage container. A storage account and its blob container must therefore be created before configuring the event subscription’s dead-letter destination. [Set dead-letter location and retry policy — Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/manage-event-delivery)

**Learn more:** [Set dead-letter location and retry policy — Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/manage-event-delivery)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Azure Blob Storage for archiving.  
  
The company requires that data in Blob Storage reside only in the archive tier.  
  
You need to ensure that data copied to Blob Storage is moved to the archive tier.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use a Put Block List operation with a request header of x-ms-immutability-policy-mode.
Create a lifecycle policy with an action of tierToArchive and configure daysAfterModificationGreaterThan for 0.
Use a Put Blob operation with a request header of x-ms-immutability-policy-until-date.
Create a lifecycle policy with an action of tierToArchive and configure a filter for blobIndexMatch.

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management can transition eligible block blobs to the archive access tier through the `tierToArchive` action. Setting `daysAfterModificationGreaterThan` to `0` makes blobs eligible immediately after their last modification, which includes copying data into Blob Storage. Immutability-policy headers do not set an access tier, and a blob-index filter only determines which blobs a lifecycle rule targets.

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management policy structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-structure) · [Lifecycle management policies that transition blobs between tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-access-tiers)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company's Azure subscription contains an Azure Log Analytics workspace.  
  
Your company has a hundred on-premises servers running either Windows Server 2012 R2 or Windows Server 2016, and they are connected to the Azure Log Analytics workspace. The Azure Log Analytics workspace is configured to collect security-related performance counters from these connected servers.  
  
You must configure alerts based on the data collected by the Azure Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You must ensure that alert rules support dimensions and that alert-creation time is minimized. In addition, one alert notification must be generated when an alert is created and when it is resolved.  
  
You need to use the required signal type when creating the alert rules.  
  
Which of the following options should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor metric alert rules support dimensions for monitoring separate time series and can be configured as stateful. A stateful metric alert sends a notification when it fires and another when the condition resolves. Activity Log alerts monitor Azure activity-log events rather than performance-counter metrics.

**Learn more:** [Create Azure Monitor metric alert rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-create-metric-alert-rule) · [Overview of Azure Monitor alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing several APIs hosted in Azure API Management (APIM).  
  
The APIs must meet these requirements:  
  
- Require a subscription key to access every API.  
- Include terms of use that subscribers must accept to use the APIs.  
- Require administrators to review and either approve or reject subscription attempts.  
- Limit the number of simultaneous subscriptions.  
  
You need to implement the APIs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure and apply query string-based versioning.
Add a new revision to all APIs. Make the revisions current and add a change log entry.

questions.explanation:
An Azure API Management product groups APIs and provides product-level subscription controls. A published, protected product can require a subscription key, present terms of use for subscriber acceptance, require administrator approval of subscription requests, and set a limit on simultaneous subscriptions.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/products - Bicep, ARM template & Terraform AzAPI reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.apimanagement/service/products) · [Tutorial - Create and publish a product in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/azure/api-management/api-management-howto-add-products)

You are building a .NET web application that stores data in Azure Cosmos DB. The application must use the Core API and support millions of read and write operations.  
  
The Azure Cosmos DB account was created with multiple write regions enabled. The application is deployed in the East US2 and Central US regions.  
  
You need to modify the application to support multi-region writes.  
  
Which two actions could accomplish this goal? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Update the ConnectionPolicy class for the Cosmos client and populate the PreferredLocations property based on the geo-proximity of the application.
Update Azure Cosmos DB to use the Strong consistency level. Add indexed properties to the container to indicate region.
Update the ConnectionPolicy class for the Cosmos client and set the UseMultipleWriteLocations property to true.
Create and deploy a custom conflict resolution policy.
Update Azure Cosmos DB to use the Session consistency level. Send the SessionToken property value from the FeedResponse object of the write action to the end-user by using a cookie.

questions.explanation:
For the .NET Core API SDK v2, multi-region writes are enabled on the client by setting `ConnectionPolicy.UseMultipleWriteLocations` to `true`. The client must also have regional preference established through `PreferredLocations` based on the application location, so writes are directed to a nearby writable region. The account is already configured with multiple write regions. [Configure multi-region writes in applications that use Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-multi-master)

**Learn more:** [Configure multi-region writes in applications that use Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-multi-master) · [ConnectionPolicy.UseMultipleWriteLocations Property](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.azure.documents.client.connectionpolicy.usemultiplewritelocations?view=azure-dotnet)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop and deploy a web app to Azure App Service. The Azure App Service uses a Basic plan in one region.  
  
Users report that the web app responds slowly. You must capture the full call stack to help identify code performance issues. Call-stack data must be correlated across app instances. You must minimize cost and the effect on web app users.  
  
You need to capture the telemetry.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Restart all apps in the App Service plan.
Upgrade the Azure App Service plan to Premium.
Enable the Always On setting for the app service.

questions.explanation:
Application Insights Profiler captures call stacks for slow requests and stores the results in Application Insights, enabling analysis across App Service instances. The Application Insights site extension provides the App Service telemetry integration, and Always On must be enabled for Profiler. Profiler is supported on the Basic App Service tier or higher, so a Premium upgrade is unnecessary and adds cost.

**Learn more:** [Enable the .NET Profiler for Azure App Service apps in Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/profiler/profiler) · [Monitor Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/monitor-app-service)

You are developing an application that uses keys held in Azure Key Vault.  
  
You need to enforce a particular cryptographic algorithm and key size for keys stored in the vault.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Policy can enforce Key Vault key requirements through policies that restrict allowed cryptographic key types and require a specified minimum RSA key size, using effects such as Deny or Audit.\

**Learn more:** [Integrate Azure Key Vault with Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/azure-policy)

You administer an Azure Storage account named `storage1`.  
  
You plan to upload 1 million blobs to `storage1`.  
  
You must assign key-value pairs to the blobs so that both the keys and values are automatically indexed and searchable through the built-in services of `storage1`.  
  
You need to run a command to assign the key-value pairs.  
  
Which command should you run?

options.text: az storage blob directory metadata update

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob index tags store key-value pairs on individual blobs and are automatically indexed for searching and filtering. The Azure CLI command that sets these tags is `az storage blob tag set`.

**Learn more:** [Use blob index tags to manage and find data on Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-index-how-to) · [az storage blob tag](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/storage/blob/tag?view=azure-cli-latest)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team is building a new REST API that will store data in Azure Blob storage. You plan to deploy the API to Azure App Service.  
  
Developers need access to the Azure Blob storage account to develop the API for the next two months. After that two-month period, the developers must no longer be able to access the Azure Blob storage account.  
  
You need to provide developers access to the Azure Blob storage account.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Generate a shared access signature (SAS) for the Azure Blob storage account and provide the SAS to all developers.
Create and apply a new lifecycle management policy to include a last accessed date value. Apply the policy to the Azure Blob storage account.
Provide all developers with the access key for the Azure Blob storage account. Update the API to include the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) timestamp for the request header.
Grant all developers access to the Azure Blob storage account by assigning role-based access control (RBAC) roles.

questions.explanation:
A shared access signature (SAS) delegates restricted access to Azure Storage for a specified time period and with specified permissions. Issuing a SAS that expires after two months provides the required temporary access without granting developers permanent storage-account credentials. Lifecycle policies manage stored data, and storage account keys provide broad access without this time-bound delegation.

**Learn more:** [Grant limited access to Azure Storage resources using shared access signatures (SAS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview) · [Delegate access by using a shared access signature](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/delegate-access-with-shared-access-signature)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution:  
  
- Create a new Azure AD application. In the application's manifest, define application roles that correspond to the required permission levels for the application.  
- Assign the appropriate Azure AD group to each role. In the website, use the `roles` claim value from the user's JWT to determine permissions.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID application roles support role-based authorization: roles can be defined for an application, assigned to groups, and included in a signed-in user’s token through the `roles` claim. The application can authorize the user based on that claim, which maps Azure AD group membership to the required permission levels.

**Learn more:** [Add app roles and get them from a token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-add-app-roles-in-apps) · [Configure group claims and app roles in tokens](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/develop/configure-tokens-group-claims-app-roles)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure the Azure Web App that hosts the website to permit only authenticated requests and require Azure AD sign-in.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Requiring Microsoft Entra ID authentication blocks unauthenticated requests, but it does not map Azure AD group membership to the admin, normal, and reader permission levels. Role- or group-specific authorization must evaluate the authenticated user’s claims.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authentication and authorization in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-authentication-authorization) · [Work with user identities in Azure App Service authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-authentication-user-identities)

questions.question:
Solution:  
  
- Create a new Azure AD application. In the application manifest, set the `groupMembershipClaims` option value to `All`.  
- In the website, use the `groups` claim value from the user's JWT to determine permissions.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The `groupMembershipClaims` manifest setting configures the `groups` claim issued in a user token. A value of `All` includes the signed-in user's group memberships, enabling the website to assign its permission levels from the group identifiers in the JWT.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand the app manifest (Microsoft Graph format)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-microsoft-graph-app-manifest) · [Configure group claims for applications by using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-fed-group-claims)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a workspace-based Azure Application Insights resource named Insights1 and an on-premises website. Internet access to the website is blocked. You plan to implement availability testing for the website by using Insights1. The implementation must maximize security while minimizing maintenance effort. You need to determine which Application Insights availability test to use to provide the required functionality.  
  
Which availability test should you use?
questions.explanation:
Public Application Insights availability tests require an HTTP or HTTPS endpoint that is reachable from the public internet. For an internal or no-ingress endpoint, availability checks must run from within the network and send their results to Application Insights through the `TrackAvailability()` API. This retains the website’s blocked internet access.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

options.text: Create an Azure App Service API and implement the change feed estimator of the SDK. Scale the API by using multiple Azure App Service instances.
Create a background job in an Azure Kubernetes Service and implement the change feed feature of the SDK.
Create an Azure Function to use a trigger for Azure Cosmos DB. Configure the trigger to connect to the container.

Create an Azure Function that uses a FeedIterator object that processes the change feed by using the pull model on the container. Use a FeedRange object to parallelize the processing of the change feed across multiple functions.

questions.explanation:
The Azure Cosmos DB trigger for Azure Functions uses the change feed processor internally, detects inserts and updates in the monitored container, and automatically parallelizes processing across container partitions. The change feed pull model can also process changes in parallel by obtaining FeedRange values and using a FeedIterator for each range across multiple function instances; the function code can write each processed change to Azure Blob Storage. The change feed estimator reports outstanding work but does not consume or process the change feed.

**Learn more:** [Read the Azure Cosmos DB change feed](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/read-change-feed) · [Serverless event-based architectures with Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/nosql/change-feed-functions)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application includes an Azure Web App and several Azure Function apps. Application secrets, including connection strings and certificates, are kept in Azure Key Vault.  
  
Secrets must not be stored in the application or its runtime environment. Changes to Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) must be kept to a minimum.  
  
You need to design how application secrets are loaded.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a single user-assigned Managed Identity with permission to access Key Vault and configure each App Service to use that Managed Identity.
Create a single Azure AD Service Principal with permission to access Key Vault and use a client secret from within the App Services to access Key Vault.
Create a system assigned Managed Identity in each App Service with permission to access Key Vault.
Create an Azure AD Service Principal with Permissions to access Key Vault for each App Service and use a certificate from within the App Services to access Key Vault.

questions.explanation:
A user-assigned managed identity can be assigned to multiple Azure App Service resources and authorized to read the required Azure Key Vault secrets. Managed identities obtain tokens without application-managed client secrets or certificates, and sharing one user-assigned identity avoids creating and authorizing a separate Microsoft Entra identity for each app.

**Learn more:** [Use managed identities for App Service and Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-managed-identity) · [Use Key Vault References as App Settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-key-vault-references)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You build Azure solutions.  
  
You must connect to a globally distributed No-SQL database by using the .NET API.  
  
You need to create an object that configures and executes requests in the database.  
  
Which code segment should you use?
questions.explanation:
`CosmosClient` is the Azure Cosmos DB .NET SDK’s account-level client for configuring and executing requests. Its constructor accepts the account endpoint URI and account key; `Database` and `Container` are resource objects accessed through that client.

You have an Azure Service Bus namespace that contains a partitioned queue named `queue1`.  
  
You plan to send a high volume of messages through `queue1` during the next few weeks. Message order will be random. You must minimize the chance that transient failures in individual partitions interrupt message transmission.  
  
You need to use the optimal partition-key configuration for the messages.  
  
Which configuration should you use?

options.text: Set the partition key of messages to the message ID value.
Enable sessions. Set the partition key of messages to the session ID value.
Enable sessions. Ensure that the partition key is different from the session ID value.
Leave the partition key value as null.

questions.explanation:
Leaving the partition key unset lets Azure Service Bus distribute messages among partitions and retry another partition when the initially selected partition is temporarily unavailable. A set partition key, including a session ID, pins messages to one partition and can cause errors if that partition is unavailable. Sessions are unnecessary because ordered delivery is not required.

**Learn more:** [Partitioned queues and topics - Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-partitioning)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Application Insights resource named AI1 and an Azure App Service web app named App1.  
  
You create a Standard availability test in AI1 and configure its URL to target App1.  
  
You need to make sure that every failed test sends email notifications to the subscription owners.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Application Insights availability tests have an associated availability alert rule, but email delivery is configured through an Azure Monitor action group. An action group can define email notifications for the Azure Resource Manager **Owner** role at the subscription scope, so attaching that action group to the availability alert sends notifications when the test fails.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability) · [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an app that stores globally distributed data across several Azure Blob Storage containers. Each container contains multiple blobs in which every app instance stores data. You enable blob versioning and soft delete.  
  
App testing and faulty code have often corrupted data. App development must support restoring data to a previous day for testing.  
  
You need to configure the storage account to support point-in-time restore.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable the change feed on the storage account to begin capturing and recording changes.
Configure object replication and specify replication rules.
Create a snapshot of the blob in the hot tier.
Configure an immutability policy that is scoped to a blob version.

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage point-in-time restore requires blob soft delete, blob versioning, and the change feed. With soft delete and versioning already enabled, the storage account must enable the change feed so it captures the blob changes needed to restore block blobs to an earlier point in time.

**Learn more:** [Perform a point-in-time restore on block blob data - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/point-in-time-restore-manage) · [Point-in-time restore for block blobs - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/point-in-time-restore-overview)

questions.question:
You administer an Azure Storage account called `storage1`.  
  
You intend to load 1 million blobs into `storage1`.  
  
You must apply key-value pairs to the blobs so that both the keys and values are automatically indexed and searchable through the built-in services of `storage1`.  
  
You need to run a command that assigns the key-value pairs.  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blob index tags are key-value attributes that Azure Storage automatically indexes, allowing blobs to be located by tag expressions. `Set-AzStorageBlobTag` assigns those blob index tags.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use blob index tags to manage and find blobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-manage-find-blobs)

questions.question:
Solution: Create an Azure Event Grid. Configure event filtering to evaluate the device identifier.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid filters and routes events to subscribed handlers; advanced filters can evaluate fields in event data. It does not itself provide device telemetry ingestion or store POS payloads in Azure Blob Storage, so configuring a device-identifier filter does not meet the data-receipt and storage requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [How to filter events for Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/how-to-filter-events) · [Event filtering for Azure Event Grid namespaces](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/namespace-event-filtering)

questions.question:
Solution: Provision an Azure Service Bus. Configure a topic to receive the device data by using a correlation filter.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus correlation filters are configured as rules on topic subscriptions, where they select messages based on message properties. They do not configure a topic itself to receive or correlate incoming device data; therefore, this configuration does not meet the ingestion requirement. [Azure Service Bus topic filters and actions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/topic-filters)\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus topic filters and actions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/topic-filters) · [Azure Service Bus queues, topics, and subscriptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-queues-topics-subscriptions)

questions.question:
Solution: Create an Azure Notification Hub and register every device with the hub.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Notification Hubs delivers push notifications from a backend to registered devices; it is not a data-ingestion service and does not receive POS telemetry for storage in Azure Blob Storage. [Azure Notification Hubs documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/notification-hubs/)\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Notification Hubs documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/notification-hubs/)

questions.question:
Solution: Provision Azure Event Grid. Configure the machine identifier as the partition key and enable capture.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Hubs, rather than Azure Event Grid, provides partition keys for correlating related device events and the Capture feature that automatically writes streaming data to Azure Blob Storage. Azure Event Grid cannot be configured with Event Hubs Capture, so this solution does not provide the required device-data ingestion and storage capability.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop an app that enables users to upload photos and videos to Azure storage. The app uses a Storage REST API call to upload media to a blob storage account named Account1. You have blob storage containers named Container1 and Container2.  
  
Video uploads happen on an irregular basis.  
  
You need to copy particular blobs from Container1 to Container2 whenever a new video is uploaded.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Copy blobs to Container2 by using the Put Blob operation of the Blob Service REST API
Create an Event Grid topic that uses the Start-AzureStorageBlobCopy cmdlet
Use AzCopy with the Snapshot switch to copy blobs to Container2
Download the blob to a virtual machine and then upload the blob to Container2

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage emits the `Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated` Event Grid event when a blob is created or replaced through Blob REST APIs. An Event Grid-triggered handler can initiate a server-side blob copy for the qualifying uploaded video, so copying occurs in response to each irregular upload without polling or transferring the blob through a virtual machine.

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob Storage as an Event Grid source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-schema-blob-storage) · [Copy Blob (REST API)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/copy-blob)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a solution that enables smart refrigerators to send temperature data to a central location.  
  
The solution must receive and retain messages until they are processed. You create an Azure Service Bus instance by specifying a name, pricing tier, subscription, resource group, and location.  
  
You need to finish the configuration.  
  
Which Azure CLI or PowerShell command should you run?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus queues provide durable message storage that decouples senders from receivers until a consumer processes each message. Creating the required queue in the existing `fridge-ns` namespace is accomplished with `New-AzureRmServiceBusQueue` using the resource group, namespace, and queue name parameters. Microsoft’s current `New-AzServiceBusQueue` documentation describes the equivalent cmdlet and required queue, namespace, and resource-group parameters.

**Learn more:** [New-AzServiceBusQueue (Az.ServiceBus)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.servicebus/new-azservicebusqueue?view=azps-16.0.0) · [Azure Service Bus queues, topics, and subscriptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-queues-topics-subscriptions)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a collection of RESTful APIs that external partners will consume.  
  
You must securely expose the APIs through Azure API Management and meet these requirements:  
  
- Only authenticated and authorized clients can access the APIs.  
- Implement control over the number of API calls to prevent abuse and ensure fair use.  
- Perform data transformation and validation for incoming requests and outgoing responses without changing the back-end services.  
- Collect insights into API usage patterns, performance metrics, and anomaly detection.  
  
You need to implement the APIs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use basic authentication over HTTPS.Apply IP filtering policies.Perform transformation logic in the client application.Enable Azure diagnostics logs.
Use OAuth 2.0 for authentication and authorization.Apply rate limit policies.Use inbound and outbound policies for transformation.Enable Azure Monitor for detailed analytics.
Require clients to present client certificates.Use response caching policies.Implement request and response transformation in back-end services.Analyze logs with Log Analytics.
Use subscription keys for authentication.Implement caching policies.Modify API code for transformation.Use Application insights for monitoring.

questions.explanation:
OAuth 2.0 provides token-based authorization for API access, and Azure API Management can validate those tokens. Rate-limit policies restrict request frequency to protect services and promote fair use. Inbound and outbound API Management policies execute at the gateway, enabling request validation and transformations of requests or responses without modifying back-end services. Azure Monitor collects and analyzes API Management telemetry for usage and performance monitoring.

**Learn more:** [Authentication and authorization to APIs in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/authentication-authorization-overview) · [Policies in Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-howto-policies)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must secure the Azure Functions to satisfy the security requirements.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer forms part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Store the RSA-HSM key in Azure Key Vault with soft-delete and purge-protection features enabled.
Store the RSA-HSM key in Azure Blob storage with an immutability policy applied to the container.
Create a free tier Azure App Configuration instance with a new Azure AD service principal.
Create a standard tier Azure App Configuration instance with an assigned Azure AD managed identity.
Store the RSA-HSM key in Azure Cosmos DB. Apply the built-in policies for customer-managed keys and allowed locations.

questions.explanation:
Azure App Configuration customer-managed encryption uses a Key Vault RSA or RSA-HSM key and requires Key Vault soft-delete and purge protection. The App Configuration store also needs an assigned managed identity so it can authenticate to Key Vault and perform key wrap and unwrap operations; customer-managed keys require the Standard or Premium tier, not the Free tier.

**Learn more:** [Use customer-managed keys to encrypt Azure App Configuration data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-app-configuration/concept-customer-managed-keys)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application that uses Azure Blob Storage.  
  
The application must read transaction logs for every change made to blobs and blob metadata in the storage account for auditing. The changes must be ordered as they occurred, contain only create, update, delete, and copy operations, and be retained for compliance.  
  
You need to process the transaction logs asynchronously.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Process all Azure Blob storage events by using Azure Event Grid with a subscriber Azure Function app.
Enable the change feed on the storage account and process all changes for available events.
Process all Azure Storage Analytics logs for successful blob events.
Use the Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector API and scan the request body for successful blob events.

questions.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage change feed provides durable, immutable, read-only transaction logs for changes to blobs and blob metadata. Applications can consume the feed asynchronously, either incrementally or in batches, and retention can be configured to meet compliance requirements. The feed captures available blob change events, allowing consumers to filter to the required operation types.

**Learn more:** [Change feed in Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-change-feed) · [Process change feed in Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-change-feed-how-to)

A large retail company runs both online and physical stores. It tracks inventory levels in real time to manage stock efficiently across every location. You develop an Azure Event Grid solution to process events generated by the inventory management system deployed in Azure.  
  
You need to implement a subscription filter that dynamically adapts to seasonal shifts in product demand.  
  
Which event filter should you use?

options.text: An advanced filter using a Boolean condition that evaluates multiple data fields, including a season field within the event data
A prefix filter on the event type field that matches the current season's name
A subscription filter that uses label filter to include events tagged with seasonal promotional codes
A static subject filter that targets events with a subject ending in “/seasonal/inventory”

questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid advanced filters evaluate event-data fields with supported comparison operators, and multiple advanced filters can be combined on an event subscription. A season-related field in the event payload can therefore be used to apply flexible seasonal filtering, unlike a fixed subject suffix or an event-type prefix. [Event filters for Azure Event Grid namespace topics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/namespace-event-filtering)

**Learn more:** [Event filters for Azure Event Grid namespace topics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/namespace-event-filtering)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an Azure Function that calls external APIs by supplying an access token for the API. The access token is stored in a secret named `token` in an Azure Key Vault named `mykeyvault`.  
  
You need to ensure that the Azure Function can access the token. Which value should you store in the Azure Function App configuration?
questions.explanation:
Azure Function App settings support Azure Key Vault references using `@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=<secretUri>)`. The secret URI for secret `token` in vault `mykeyvault` is `https://mykeyvault.vault.azure.net/secrets/token/`, so this reference resolves the secret value for the function app, provided its identity has permission to read the secret.

**Learn more:** [Use Key Vault references as app settings in Azure App Service, Azure Functions, and Azure Logic Apps (Standard)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-key-vault-references)
