Your solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Read operations must never receive write operations out of order.  
- Maximize concurrency for read operations in every region.  
  
You need to select the consistency level for the solution.  
  
Which consistency level should you use?
questions.explanation:
Consistent prefix consistency ensures reads return a prefix of the committed write sequence, so writes are never observed out of order. It uses single-replica reads, which provides higher read concurrency than consistency levels that require quorum reads, such as bounded staleness.\
\
**Learn more:** [Consistency level choices - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop and deploy an ASP.NET web app to Azure App Service, using Application Insights telemetry to monitor it.  
  
You must test the app to confirm that it is available and responsive from different locations worldwide at regular intervals. If the app does not respond, an alert must be sent to support staff.  
  
You need to configure a test for the web app.  
  
Which two test types can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Application Insights availability tests run web requests at regular intervals from geographically distributed locations and can alert when an application is unavailable or responds too slowly. The applicable legacy availability-web-test types are URL ping tests for a single endpoint request and multi-step web tests for a sequence of web requests. URL ping tests are deprecated in current Azure documentation, but they remain a valid match to the supplied test-type choices.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability) · [Azure Application Insights availability monitoring FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/azure-monitor/app-insights/availability/availability-monitoring-common-issues-faq)

questions.question:
You are building a Microsoft Entra ID–integrated app that communicates with Microsoft Graph.  
  
You must enable GET operations to receive unknown members that could be defined in the future in the Microsoft Graph API. You plan to support evolvable enumerations in the app.  
  
You need to specify the HTTP request header that provides evolvable-enumeration support in the app.  
  
Which header should you specify?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Graph uses the `Prefer` request header with the value `include-unknown-enum-members` to opt in to future members of evolvable enumerations during GET operations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Best practices for working with Microsoft Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/best-practices-concept)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
You have 100 Azure virtual machines (VMs) that have system-assigned managed identity enabled.  
  
You need to determine the value of the object ID attribute for each identity.  
  
Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
A VM's system-assigned managed identity exposes its Microsoft Entra object ID as `Identity.PrincipalId`. `Get-AzVM` retrieves the VM properties, so its output can be enumerated to obtain `Identity.PrincipalId` for every VM.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get-AzVM (Az.Compute)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.compute/get-azvm?view=azps-15.6.0) · [Managed Identity Authentication for Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-authentication-managed-identity)

questions.question:
You have 100 Azure virtual machines (VMs) that have system-assigned managed identity enabled.  
  
You need to determine the value of the object ID attribute for each identity.  
  
Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
The `allkeys-lru` policy evicts the least recently used key from the entire cache, retaining cached entries for players who have moved most recently while allowing stale entries, including those for logged-out players, to be removed. Microsoft documents that `allkeys-lru` removes the least recently used key, whereas `volatile-lru` considers only keys that have an expiration set.

**Learn more:** [Configure Azure Cache for Redis — eviction policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-configure)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
You develop Azure Durable Functions to manage vehicle loans.  
  
The loan process contains multiple actions that must run in a specified order. One action is a customer credit-check process, which might take multiple days to complete.  
  
You need to implement Azure Durable Functions for the loan process.  
  
Which Azure Durable Functions type should you use?
questions.explanation:
An orchestrator function coordinates other functions as a durable, code-based workflow, allowing actions to be run in a specified sequence while preserving progress during long-running waits. Orchestration instances can run for days or longer, which supports a credit-check process that may take multiple days.\
\
**Learn more:** [Durable orchestrations - Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/durable-task/common/durable-task-orchestrations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a web application that uses the Microsoft identity platform to authenticate users and resources. The web application calls several REST APIs.  
  
A REST API request must read the user's calendar. The web application also needs permission to send email as the user.  
  
You need to authorize the web application and the API.  
  
Which parameter should you use?
questions.explanation:
The `scope` parameter requests the delegated permissions that a web application needs to access resources on behalf of a signed-in user, including permissions such as `Calendars.Read` and `Mail.Send`.

**Learn more:** [Developer’s Guide to Requesting Permissions and Consent in Microsoft Identity Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/consent-types-developer) · [Scopes and permissions in the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/scopes-oidc)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop solutions for Azure.  
  
A .NET application must receive a message whenever an Azure virtual machine completes data processing. Messages must **NOT** persist after the receiving application processes them.  
  
You need to implement the .NET object that receives the messages.  
  
Which object should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus queues support point-to-point delivery to a single consumer. A QueueClient can receive messages using ReceiveAndDelete mode, which treats messages as settled when they are delivered and removes them from the queue, so they do not remain after processing.

**Learn more:** [Message Transfers, Locks, and Settlement - Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/message-transfers-locks-settlement) · [Azure Service Bus queues, topics, and subscriptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-queues-topics-subscriptions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing several microservices to run on Azure Container Apps. External HTTP ingress traffic is enabled for the microservices.  
  
The microservices must be deployed in the same virtual network and write logs to the same Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You need to deploy the microservices.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use a separate environment for each container.
Use a private container registry image and single image for all containers.
Use a single environment for all containers.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Container Apps environment provides the shared boundary for its container apps. Container apps deployed in the same environment share the virtual network and use the same Log Analytics logging destination, so a single environment meets both requirements.

**Learn more:** [Azure Container Apps environments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/environment) · [Integrate a virtual network with an Azure Container Apps environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/vnet-custom)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application that enforces a set of governance policies for internal and external services, as well as for applications.  
  
You develop a stateful ASP.NET Core 2.1 web application named PolicyApp and deploy it to an Azure App Service Web App. PolicyApp responds to events from Azure Event Grid and performs policy actions based on those events.  
  
You have the following requirements:  
  
- Authentication events must be used to monitor users as they sign in and sign out.  
- PolicyApp must process all authentication events.  
- Sign-outs must be processed as quickly as possible.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a new Azure Event Grid subscription for all authentication events. Use the subscription to process sign-out events.
Create a separate Azure Event Grid handler for sign-in and sign-out events.
Create separate Azure Event Grid topics and subscriptions for sign-in and sign-out events.
Add a subject prefix to sign-out events. Create an Azure Event Grid subscription. Configure the subscription to use the subjectBeginsWith filter.

questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid event subscriptions support subject-prefix filtering through `subjectBeginsWith`, which delivers only events whose subject matches the configured prefix. Giving sign-out events a distinct subject prefix and subscribing with that filter isolates them for direct, prompt processing while other authentication-event processing remains available to PolicyApp.

**Learn more:** [How to filter events for Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/how-to-filter-events)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a hazard-notification system with one signaling server that causes audio and visual alarms to start and stop.  
  
You use Azure Service Bus to publish alarms. Each alarm controller uses Azure Service Bus to receive alarm signals within a transaction. Alarm events must be logged for auditing. Each transaction record must contain information about the type of alarm that was activated.  
  
You need to implement a reply-trail auditing solution.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign the value of the hazard message SessionID property to the ReplyToSessionId property.
Assign the value of the hazard message MessageId property to the DevileryCount property.
Assign the value of the hazard message SessionID property to the SequenceNumber property.
Assign the value of the hazard message MessageId property to the CorrelationId property.
Assign the value of the hazard message SequenceNumber property to the DeliveryCount property.
Assign the value of the hazard message MessageId property to the SequenceNumber property.

questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus reply routing can use `ReplyToSessionId` to specify the session identifier for replies. A reply is correlated to its triggering message by setting the reply message's `CorrelationId` to the handled message's `MessageId`. This preserves the audit trail between the originating hazard signal and each controller response.

**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus messages, payloads, and serialization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messages-payloads)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing several microservices for deployment to a new Azure Kubernetes Service cluster. The microservices manage data stored in Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Blob storage. The data is protected by using customer-managed keys stored in Azure Key Vault.  
  
You must automate rotation for all Azure Key Vault keys while also allowing manual key rotation. Keys must be rotated every three months. Notifications for expiring keys must be sent before the keys expire.  
  
You need to configure key rotation and enable key-expiry notifications.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create and configure a new Azure Event Grid instance.
Create and assign an Azure Key Vault access policy.
Create and configure a key rotation policy during key creation.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Key Vault key rotation policy can schedule automatic generation of new key versions at a defined interval and still permits on-demand rotation. Its notification action triggers Azure Event Grid key-near-expiry events before expiration; configuring Event Grid enables those events to be routed to a notification handler.

**Learn more:** [Configure cryptographic key auto-rotation in Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/how-to-configure-key-rotation) · [Azure Key Vault as Event Grid source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-schema-key-vault)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to access data from the user claim object in the e-commerce web app.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Write custom code to make a Microsoft Graph API call from the e-commerce web app.
Assign the Contributor RBAC role to the e-commerce web app by using the Resource Manager create role assignment API.
Update the e-commerce web app to read the HTTP request header values.
Using the Azure CLI, enable Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) from the e-commerce checkout API to the e-commerce web app.

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service authentication exposes authenticated user claims to application code in injected HTTP request headers, such as `X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL`. The app must read those headers to obtain and process the claim data. [Work with user identities in Azure App Service authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-authentication-user-identities)

**Learn more:** [Work with user identities in Azure App Service authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-authentication-user-identities)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
Solution: Publish events to a partner topic. Create an event subscription for every customer.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid partner topics are intended for events published by a registered partner system to Azure customers. An Event Grid domain is the appropriate multi-tenant model: it represents each customer as a topic, supports Microsoft Entra ID authentication and authorization, and provides a single endpoint for publishing all customer events.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use cases for Event Domains in Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-domains-use-cases) · [Partner Events overview for customers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/partner-events-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: Publish events to an event domain and create one custom topic for each customer.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid domains provide a single publishing endpoint for thousands of customer-specific topics, making them suitable for multitenant event delivery at scale. Topic-level access can be controlled through Microsoft Entra ID and Azure RBAC, and event subscriptions support event-type filtering so only relevant events are delivered for processing.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand event domains for managing Event Grid topics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-domains) · [Publish events with event domains with Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/how-to-event-domains)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
Solution: Publish events to a custom topic, and create one event subscription for every customer.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid custom topics are limited to 500 event subscriptions per topic, and that limit cannot be increased. Creating an event subscription for each of thousands of customers therefore cannot meet the required scale, even though custom topics support a single publishing endpoint, event-type filtering, and Microsoft Entra ID-based authentication and authorization.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Event Grid quotas and limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/quotas-limits) · [Use cases for Event Domains in Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-domains-use-cases)

questions.question:
Solution: Turn on ingress, create a TCP scale rule, and apply that rule to the container app.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Container Apps TCP scale rules control replica scaling based on concurrent TCP connections. They do not create an Azure Event Grid namespace/topic or event subscriptions, which provide event-type filtering and can use Microsoft Entra ID for publishing authentication and authorization.\
\
**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app) · [Concepts for Event Grid namespace topics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/concepts-event-grid-namespaces)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
Solution: Publish events to a system topic, and create an event subscription for each customer.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid system topics are for events published by Azure services and do not expose an endpoint for an application to publish its own events. Consequently, a system topic cannot provide the required single publishing endpoint for the application, regardless of creating one event subscription per customer.\
\
**Learn more:** [System topics in Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/system-topics) · [Authenticate Event Grid publishing clients using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/authenticate-with-microsoft-entra-id)

questions.question:
Solution: Publish events to a system topic, and create an event subscription for each customer.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure API Management supports Basic authentication for a backend, which sets the HTTP `Authorization` header from the configured credentials, and client-certificate authentication for a backend, which authenticates the gateway to the HSTS-protected service by using a TLS client certificate. Digest authentication is not a supported Azure API Management backend authentication policy, while OAuth client credentials describes an OAuth grant flow rather than the applicable named backend authentication policy.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate with Basic — Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/authentication-basic-policy) · [Authenticate with client certificate — Azure API Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/authentication-certificate-policy)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing applications for a company and plan to host them on Azure App Services.  
  
The company has these requirements:  
  
- Every five minutes, check that the websites are responsive.  
- Confirm that the websites respond within a specified time threshold. Dependent requests, such as images and JavaScript files, must load correctly.  
- Generate alerts when a website is experiencing issues.  
- If a website does not load, attempt to reload it three additional times.  
  
You need to implement this process with the least effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a Selenium web test and configure it to run from your workstation as a scheduled task.
Set up a URL ping test to query the home page.
Create an Azure function to query the home page.
Create a multi-step web test to query the home page.
Create a Custom Track Availability Test to query the home page.

questions.explanation:
An Application Insights URL ping availability test provides scheduled HTTP availability checks, response-time thresholds, dependent-request parsing, alerting, and configurable retries. It meets the home-page monitoring requirements without the custom code or maintenance required by Selenium, an Azure Function, or a custom TrackAvailability implementation.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

questions.question:
You need to implement aggregated telemetry values for distributor API calls.  
  
Which Application Insights API method should you use?
questions.explanation:
`TrackMetric` records numeric custom metrics and supports sending aggregated metric values for a time period. Aggregation reduces the number of telemetry data points sent while retaining the statistics needed to analyze API-value trends.\
\
**Learn more:** [TelemetryClient.TrackMetric Method](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.applicationinsights.telemetryclient.trackmetric?view=azure-dotnet) · [Metrics in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/metrics-overview)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure authentication for farmers.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add the shared access signature (SAS) token to the app.
Create a shared access signature (SAS) token.
Add the app to the user flow.
Register the app in Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra External ID authentication requires registering the application, creating a user flow to define the farmer sign-up/sign-in experience, and adding the registered application to that user flow. A shared access signature (SAS) grants delegated access to Azure resources and is unrelated to Microsoft Entra interactive user authentication.

**Learn more:** [Add your application to the user flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/how-to-user-flow-add-application) · [Create a sign-up and sign-in user flow for an external tenant app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/how-to-user-flow-sign-up-sign-in-customers)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure every site configuration setting for the corporate website.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Update the role assignments for the Azure Key Vault.
Create an Azure App Configuration store.
Update the role assignments for the Azure App Configuration store.

questions.explanation:
Azure App Configuration centrally manages application settings. An App Service managed identity can authenticate to the store without application secrets, and assigning that identity the App Configuration Data Reader role grants least-privilege read access to the configuration values.

**Learn more:** [Use App Configuration references for Azure App Service and Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-configuration-references) · [Use managed identities to access App Configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-app-configuration/howto-integrate-azure-managed-service-identity)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to secure the corporate website so that it meets the security requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an Azure Cache for Redis instance. Update the code to support the cache.
Create an Azure Content Delivery Network profile and endpoint. Configure the endpoint.С. Create an App Service instance with a standard plan. Configure the custom domain with a TLS/SSL certificate.
Create an Azure Application Gateway with a Web Application Firewall (WAF). Configure end-to-end TLS encryption and the WAF.

questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway with Web Application Firewall (WAF) can provide end-to-end TLS encryption between clients, the gateway, and the backend. Its WAF supports geo-match custom rules that restrict web-application access by country or region, satisfying both the HTTPS/TLS and geographic-content-restriction requirements.

**Learn more:** [Enabling end-to-end TLS on Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/ssl-overview) · [Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) Geomatch custom rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/geomatch-custom-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a gateway solution for a public-facing news API. The news API backend is implemented as a RESTful service and uses an OpenAPI specification.  
  
You must ensure that the news API can be accessed by using an Azure API Management service instance.  
  
Which Azure PowerShell command should you run?
questions.explanation:
Importing the REST API's OpenAPI/Swagger specification into Azure API Management creates the API definition and its operations in the APIM service. `Import-AzureRmApiManagementApi` with `-SpecificationFormat "Swagger"`, `-SpecificationPath`, and `-Path` performs that import; it is the AzureRM predecessor of the current `Import-AzApiManagementApi` cmdlet.

**Learn more:** [Import-AzApiManagementApi (Az.ApiManagement)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.apimanagement/import-azapimanagementapi)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure Azure Event Hubs to receive events from Azure services. Create a custom Azure Functions application using Event Hub triggers to process the events. Add custom filtering logic within the functions to choose the relevant events.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid is designed to route Azure service events, filter subscriptions by event type or event attributes, reliably retry delivery, and invoke Azure Functions as an event handler. Implementing filtering inside Event Hub-triggered functions adds custom routing and filtering code, so it does not meet the requirement to minimize custom code for event routing and handling.\
\
**Learn more:** [Introduction to Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/overview) · [How to filter events for Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/how-to-filter-events)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure Azure Event Hubs to receive events from Azure services. Create a custom Azure Functions application using Event Hub triggers to process the events. Add custom filtering logic within the functions to choose the relevant events.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Logic Apps polling is interval-based and does not provide the event-driven routing, subscription-level filtering, and durable retry delivery required to reliably process high-volume Azure service events while a processing application is temporarily unavailable. Azure Event Grid is designed for high-throughput event routing, filtering by event attributes, and retry-based delivery to handlers such as Azure Functions.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/overview) · [Azure Event Grid message delivery and retry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/delivery-and-retry)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: Configure Azure Event Grid system topics for every Azure service. Create event subscriptions that use Advanced Filters to receive only relevant events. Use Azure Functions with Event Grid triggers to process the events. Enable dead-lettering on the event subscriptions to handle failures and provide reliable delivery.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid system topics and event subscriptions provide managed event routing for supported Azure services. Subscription filters limit delivery to relevant event types, subjects, or event properties, while Azure Functions Event Grid triggers provide serverless event processing. Event Grid uses at-least-once delivery and retries failed deliveries; dead-lettering stores events that remain undeliverable after the configured retry policy, preserving them for recovery.

**Learn more:** [Azure Event Grid message delivery and retry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/delivery-and-retry) · [Azure Event Grid trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-event-grid-trigger)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Grid provides managed, high-volume event routing from Azure event sources, advanced filtering by event type and event attributes, durable delivery and retries, and direct Azure Functions event handling. Azure Service Bus sessions and message deferral are brokered-message features; they do not provide the required Azure-service event routing and filtering, and they require additional handling logic.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/overview) · [Azure Event Grid message delivery and retry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/delivery-and-retry)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop solutions on Azure.  
  
You need to connect to a globally distributed NoSQL database by using the .NET API.  
  
You must create an object that configures and executes requests in the database.  
  
Which code segment should you use?
questions.explanation:
`CosmosClient` is the Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL .NET SDK client object that provides a client-side representation of the service and is used to configure and execute service requests. Constructing it with the account endpoint and key creates the required client. [Microsoft Learn: Get started using .NET](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-dotnet-get-started)

**Learn more:** [Get started using .NET - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-dotnet-get-started) · [CosmosClient Class (Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.azure.cosmos.cosmosclient?view=azure-dotnet)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an Azure messaging solution.  
  
You must ensure that the solution meets these requirements:  
  
- Provide transactional support.  
- Provide duplicate detection.  
- Retain messages for an unlimited time period.  
  
Which two technologies meet the requirements? Each correct answer represents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus queues and topics support transactional operations and broker-side duplicate detection. In the Standard and Premium tiers, their default message time-to-live can be set to the maximum signed 64-bit value, which provides effectively unlimited message retention. Azure Storage Queue supports non-expiring messages but does not provide these Service Bus transaction and duplicate-detection capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Azure Service Bus Messaging](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview) · [Enable duplicate message detection - Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/enable-duplicate-detection)

You are a developer at a company that recently moved to workspace-based Application Insights for a C# .NET web application running on Azure.  
  
The application experiences intermittent performance problems.  
  
You need to use the AI-powered code-analysis capability in Application Insights to help diagnose the issue.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use the Application Map to visualize dependencies and interactions, then trace the performance issues through the map.
Enable the profiler and snapshot debugger.
Configure continuous export of telemetry data to Azure Storage.

questions.explanation:
Application Insights Code Optimizations is an AI-based service that works with Application Insights Profiler to analyze .NET runtime behavior and provide code-level performance recommendations. Enabling the profiler collects traces showing where execution time is spent; Snapshot Debugger adds code-level diagnostic context for production issues.

**Learn more:** [Monitor and analyze runtime behavior with Code Optimizations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/optimization-insights/code-optimizations-vs-extension) · [Azure CLI: az monitor app-insights component connect-webapp](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/monitor/app-insights/component?view=azure-cli-latest)

You have a workspace-based Azure Application Insights resource named Insights1 and an Azure App Service Web App named App1. Insights1 gathers telemetry generated by App1.  
  
You plan to test App1 availability by using Insights1. The test must perform the following tasks:  
  
- Parse dependent requests.  
- Validate TLS certificates.  
- Configure custom request headers.  
  
You must minimize development and implementation effort.  
  
You need to implement the Application Insights availability test that provides the required functionality.  
  
Which availability test should you implement?
questions.explanation:
Application Insights Standard tests natively support parsing dependent requests, validating TLS/SSL certificate validity, and configuring custom HTTP request headers. They satisfy all requirements through built-in configuration, minimizing development and implementation effort.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

questions.question:
Solution: Process the blob data by using the Durable Functions async pattern.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Durable Functions asynchronous pattern returns an immediate response while a durable orchestration performs the longer-running blob-processing work. Azure Functions documentation specifically recommends this pattern for processing that exceeds an HTTP-triggered function’s response-time limit.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Functions scale and hosting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-scale) · [HTTP features in Durable Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/durable-task/durable-functions/durable-functions-http-features)

questions.question:
Solution: Send the HTTP trigger payload to an Azure Service Bus queue for processing by a queue-triggered function, and return an immediate successful HTTP response.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Functions must return an HTTP-triggered response within 230 seconds, irrespective of the configured function timeout. Deferring the payload to an Azure Service Bus queue allows a queue-triggered function to process it asynchronously while the HTTP function returns immediately, avoiding the HTTP timeout.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Functions HTTP trigger](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-http-webhook-trigger) · [Compare Azure Functions runtime versions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-versions)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure the app to run on an App Service hosting plan and turn on the **Always On** setting.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Always On prevents a Dedicated-plan function app from becoming idle, but it does not extend the maximum HTTP response duration. Azure Functions documents a 230-second maximum for an HTTP-triggered function to respond, irrespective of the configured function timeout; long-running work should be deferred or handled through an asynchronous pattern.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Functions runtime versions overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-versions) · [Azure Functions Dedicated hosting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/dedicated-plan)

questions.question:
Solution: Change the `functionTimeout` property in the `host.json` project file to 10 minutes.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An HTTP-triggered Azure Function must respond within 230 seconds because of the Azure Load Balancer idle timeout, regardless of the `functionTimeout` value. A longer-running workload should use an asynchronous pattern or return an immediate response while processing continues.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Functions runtime versions overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-versions) · [Azure Functions HTTP trigger](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-http-webhook-trigger)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to investigate an Azure Function app error message in the development environment.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Connect Live Metrics Stream from Application Insights to the Azure Function app and filter the metrics.
Create a new Azure Log Analytics workspace and instrument the Azure Function app with Application Insights.
Update the Azure Function app with extension methods from Microsoft.Extensions.Logging to log events by using the log instance.
Add a new diagnostic setting to the Azure Function app to send logs to Log Analytics.

questions.explanation:
Application Insights Live Metrics Stream displays Azure Function app logs and metrics in near real time. Its filtering capability isolates the telemetry from the relevant app, enabling investigation of the error without changing the app’s logging or diagnostic configuration.

You manage an Azure App Service web app named App1 and a related Azure Application Insights resource named AppInsights1.  
  
You need alerts for any unusual increase in the rate of failed HTTP requests directed at App1.  
  
You need to implement push notifications.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures AppInsights1.
From the Azure portal, modify an action group of Azure Monitor.
From the Azure portal, modify diagnostic settings of AppInsights1.
Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures the analyticsItems child resource of AppInsights1.

questions.explanation:
Application Insights Smart Detection detects Failure Anomalies—unusual increases in failed HTTP request rates. Azure Monitor action groups define the notification actions for alerts, including push notification delivery; therefore, modifying the relevant action group configures the required notification behavior. Diagnostic settings are for routing telemetry data, not alert notifications.

**Learn more:** [Smart detection in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/proactive-diagnostics) · [Smart Detection of Failure Anomalies in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/proactive-failure-diagnostics)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop a website and plan to host it in Azure. You anticipate that the website will experience high traffic volumes after it is published.  
  
You must ensure that the website stays available and responsive while minimizing cost.  
  
You need to deploy the website. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the website to a virtual machine. Configure the virtual machine to automatically scale when the CPU load is high.
Deploy the website to an App Service that uses the Shared service tier. Configure the App Service plan to automatically scale when the CPU load is high.
Deploy the website to a virtual machine. Configure a Scale Set to increase the virtual machine instance count when the CPU load is high.
Deploy the website to an App Service that uses the Standard service tier. Configure the App Service plan to automatically scale when the CPU load is high.

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service Standard supports autoscale rules based on metrics such as CPU utilization and can scale out to multiple dedicated instances. The Shared tier cannot scale out, while a single virtual machine does not provide scale-out availability. A Standard App Service plan supplies managed web hosting and adds instances only when load requires it, supporting responsiveness and cost control.

**Learn more:** [Azure App Service plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plans) · [Plan and manage costs for Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-manage-costs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop Azure Web Apps for a commercial diving company. Regulations require every diver to complete a health questionnaire every 15 days after each diving job begins.  
  
You need to configure the Azure Web Apps so the instance count scales out while divers are completing the questionnaire and scales in once they finish.  
  
You need to configure autoscaling.  
  
Which two autoscaling configurations could achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
CPU usage-based autoscaling can add instances when questionnaire activity increases CPU utilization and remove instances after utilization decreases. A fixed date and time autoscale profile can apply scaling rules and capacity limits for a specified questionnaire window 15 days after a known job start. Recurring profiles repeat on selected days of the week, whereas predictive autoscale is supported only for Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets.

**Learn more:** [Autoscale with multiple profiles - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/autoscale/autoscale-multiprofile) · [Use predictive autoscale to scale out before load demands in virtual machine scale sets - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/autoscale/autoscale-predictive)

Your company has an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to deploy several Azure virtual machines to the subscription by using Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates. The virtual machines will be part of one availability set.  
  
You need to ensure that the ARM template enables as many virtual machines as possible to remain accessible during a fabric failure or maintenance event.  
  
Which value should you configure for the `platformUpdateDomainCount` property?
questions.explanation:
Update domains are groups of virtual machines and underlying hardware that can be restarted simultaneously during planned maintenance; Azure restarts only one update domain at a time. An availability set supports up to 20 update domains, so configuring `platformUpdateDomainCount` as 20 provides the greatest distribution for maintenance availability.

**Learn more:** [Availability sets overview - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/availability-set-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a solution that enables smart refrigerators to send temperature data to a central location.  
  
The solution must receive and retain messages until they are processed. You create an Azure Service Bus instance by supplying a name, pricing tier, subscription, resource group, and location.  
  
You need to finish the configuration.  
  
Which Azure CLI or PowerShell command should you run?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Service Bus queue receives and stores messages until consumers process them. `New-AzServiceBusQueue` creates a queue in the existing `fridge-ns` namespace and supports the resource group, queue name, and `-EnablePartitioning` parameters shown.

**Learn more:** [New-AzServiceBusQueue (Az.ServiceBus)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.servicebus/new-azservicebusqueue?view=azps-15.3.0)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an ASP.NET Core app hosted in Azure App Service.  
  
The app needs Microsoft Entra ID to return custom claims for user authorization. Those claims must be removed if the app registration is removed.  
  
You need to add the custom claims to the user's access token.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Require the https://graph.microsoft.com/.default scope during authentication.
Configure the app to use the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow.
Implement custom middleware to retrieve role information from Azure AD.
Add the groups to the groupMembershipClaims attribute in the app manifest.
Add the roles to the appRoles attribute in the app manifest.

questions.explanation:
Application roles declared in the app registration's `appRoles` attribute are application-defined authorization values. When a user or group is assigned an app role, Microsoft Entra ID includes that role in the `roles` claim of an access token issued for the application API. The role definitions are owned by the app registration, so they are removed with that registration.

**Learn more:** [Add app roles and get them from a token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-add-app-roles-in-apps) · [Microsoft Entra app manifest (Azure AD Graph format)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-app-manifest)

questions.question:
Solution: Authenticate the VM to Azure Resource Manager by using an X.509 certificate.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An X.509 certificate can authenticate a Microsoft Entra service principal, which can be assigned Azure RBAC roles at resource-group scope and obtain an access token for Azure Resource Manager.\
\
**Learn more:** [Sign in with Azure CLI using a service principal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/authenticate-azure-cli-service-principal?view=azure-cli-latest) · [Create an Azure app identity (PowerShell)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-authenticate-service-principal-powershell)

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services
questions.question:
Solution: Authenticate the VM with Azure Resource Manager by using the Reader role-based access control (RBAC) role.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: The Reader RBAC role grants read-only authorization after an identity has authenticated and acquired a token. It cannot authenticate a virtual machine or issue an Azure Resource Manager access token; the VM needs a managed identity or another supported authentication method.

questions.question:
Solution: Use the `Invoke-RestMethod` cmdlet to send a request to the local managed identity for Azure resources endpoint.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A virtual machine’s managed identity can obtain an Azure Resource Manager access token by sending an `Invoke-RestMethod` request to the local managed-identity endpoint and specifying the Azure Resource Manager resource URI. The identity’s access to particular resource groups is controlled separately by its Azure RBAC role assignments.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use managed identities on a virtual machine to acquire an access token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-to-use-vm-token)

questions.question:
An organization hosts web apps in Azure and uses Azure Monitor.  
  
You find that configuration changes have been made to some of the web apps. You need to identify those configuration changes.  
  
Which Azure Monitor log should you review?
questions.explanation:
Configuration changes are audit and control-plane events, not application log entries or console output. Among the listed App Service tables, `AppServiceAuditLogs` is the audit-log option intended to support investigation of changes. `AppServiceEnvironmentPlatformLogs` is specific to an App Service Environment, which is not specified.\
\
**Learn more:** [Monitor Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/monitor-app-service) · [Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/diagnostic-settings)

questions.question:
Solution:  
  
1. Create an Azure Cosmos DB database with Storage Service Encryption turned on.  
2. Save the intake forms in the Azure Cosmos DB database.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Storage Service Encryption protects data while it is stored, not after it is retrieved by a party with access. Azure Cosmos DB client-side encryption (Always Encrypted) encrypts sensitive data in the client application and does not reveal plaintext or encryption keys to the database service, which is necessary to protect downloaded form contents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use client-side encryption with Always Encrypted - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-always-encrypted) · [Secure your account - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/security)

questions.question:
Solution:  
  
1. Create an Azure Key Vault key called `skey`.  
2. Encrypt the intake forms with the public-key portion of `skey`.  
3. Save the encrypted data in Azure Blob storage.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Encryption with the public portion of an asymmetric Azure Key Vault key protects confidentiality because decryption requires the corresponding private portion and Key Vault decrypt permission. Downloading the encrypted Blob data alone therefore does not expose the intake-form contents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Key types, algorithms, and operations - Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/about-keys-details) · [Decrypt - Azure Key Vault REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/keyvault/keys/decrypt/decrypt?view=rest-keyvault-keys-2025-07-01)

questions.question:
Solution: Store the intake forms as secrets in Azure Key Vault.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault is not designed to store customer documents or other general content; secrets are intended for sensitive values such as passwords, connection strings, and access keys, and each secret is limited to 25 KB. Scanned intake forms should instead be stored in an appropriate encrypted data store, such as Azure Storage, to protect their contents if downloaded by a third party.\
\
**Learn more:** [Secure your Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/secure-key-vault) · [About Azure Key Vault secrets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/secrets/about-secrets)

questions.question:
You are a developer at a SaaS company that provides many web services.  
  
All company web services must meet these requirements:  
  
- Use API Management to access the services.  
- Use OpenID Connect for authentication.  
- Prevent anonymous use.  
  
A recent security audit discovered that several web services can be invoked without authentication. Which API Management policy should you implement?
questions.explanation:
The `validate-jwt` API Management policy enforces the presence and validity of a JSON Web Token and supports an OpenID Connect configuration endpoint for issuer and signing-key metadata. It rejects requests that lack a valid token, thereby preventing anonymous access.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure API Management policy reference - validate-jwt](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/validate-jwt-policy)

options.text: Create and register a sentinel key in the App Configuration store. Set the refreshAll parameter of the Register method to true.
Increase the App Configuration cache expiration from the default value.
Decrease the App Configuration cache expiration from the default value.
Create and configure Azure Key Vault. Implement the Azure Key Vault configuration provider.
Register all keys in the App Configuration store. Set the refreshAll parameter of the Register method to false.
Create and implement environment variables for each App Configuration store setting.

questions.explanation:
A sentinel key updated only after all related settings are changed lets the Azure App Configuration provider detect one change and refresh all configuration values when `refreshAll` is `true`, preserving a consistent configuration set while avoiding monitoring every setting individually. Increasing the refresh interval/cache expiration reduces how often the provider sends change-detection requests to App Configuration; dynamic refresh remains available without restarting the application.

**Learn more:** [Azure App Configuration .NET provider reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-app-configuration/reference-dotnet-provider) · [Use dynamic configuration in an ASP.NET Core app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-app-configuration/enable-dynamic-configuration-aspnet-core)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You build an ASP. Net Care application by integrating the Application Insights SDK into your solution.  
  
The application sends telemetry at a very high rate over a short interval. You observe fewer events, traces, and metrics being recorded, along with increased telemetry-ingestion error rates. Telemetry data must synchronize client and server information to enable HTTP request and response correlation.  
  
You need to lower telemetry traffic, data costs, and storage costs while maintaining statistically correct analysis of application telemetry data.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set a daily cap on the Log Analytics workspace. Create an Activity log alert rule.
Modify the pricing tier for the Log Analytics workspace.
Verify adaptive sampling is enabled. Set the maxTelemetryItemsPerSecond value.
Set retention and archive policies by table in the Log Analytics workspace. Purge retained data beyond 30 days.

questions.explanation:
Application Insights adaptive sampling reduces telemetry at the SDK by targeting a configured maximum number of telemetry items per second. It retains sampling metadata for statistically valid aggregate analysis and applies sampling consistently to correlated telemetry, helping preserve end-to-end request correlation while reducing ingestion volume and associated costs.

A company is implementing a publish-subscribe (Pub/Sub) messaging component using Azure Service Bus. You are developing the first subscription application.  
  
In the Azure portal, you observe that messages are sent to the subscription for each topic. You create and initialize a subscription client object by providing the correct details, but the subscription application still does not consume the messages.  
  
You need to make sure that the subscription client processes every message.  
  
Which code segment should you use?
questions.explanation:
A `SubscriptionClient` receives and processes messages only after a message handler is registered. `RegisterMessageHandler` attaches the processing callback and its options, enabling delivery of subscription messages to `ProcessMessagesAsync`. Creating the client alone does not begin callback-based processing, while closing it stops processing.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for improving performance using Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-performance-improvements)

options.text: Add the path to the static content generation tool to WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE setting in the host.json file.
Add a PreBuild target in the websites csproj project file that runs the static content generation script.
Create a file named run.cmd in the folder /run that calls a script which generates the static content and deploys the website.
Create a file named .deployment in the root of the repository that calls a script which generates the static content and deploys the website.

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service continuous deployment supports deployment customization through a `.deployment` file in the repository root, which can invoke a script that generates static content before deployment completes. A project-level MSBuild `PreBuild` target can also execute the static-generation script as part of preparing the website’s build output. `WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE` is an App Service setting rather than a `host.json` setting for invoking build tools, and a `/run/run.cmd` file is not the repository-level custom deployment mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Configure continuous deployment - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-continuous-deployment) · [Configure a PHP App - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-language-php)

questions.explanation:
An Application Insights URL ping availability test makes recurring requests to a public HTTP or HTTPS endpoint, records its availability and response time, and can alert when the endpoint fails or does not respond within the configured timeout. It therefore directly monitors the REST API endpoints' availability and responsiveness. URL ping tests are deprecated, with retirement scheduled for September 30, 2026; a Standard test is the current replacement, but it is not among the available choices.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783860542542-cpoiqlx3.png)

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop an Azure App Service web app and deploy it to a production environment. You enable Application Insights for the web app.  
  
The web app throws multiple exceptions in that environment.  
  
You need to inspect the state of the source code and variables when the exceptions occur.  
  
Which Application Insights feature should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Application Insights Snapshot Debugger automatically captures debug snapshots when exceptions occur in supported live .NET applications, including Azure App Service. These snapshots let you inspect the call stack, source-code location, local variables, and parameters associated with the exception.

**Learn more:** [Debug exceptions in .NET applications using Snapshot Debugger](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/snapshot-debugger/snapshot-debugger) · [View Application Insights Snapshot Debugger data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/snapshot-debugger/snapshot-debugger-data)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a Java application that uses Cassandra to store key-value data. You plan to use a new Azure Cosmos DB resource and the Cassandra API in the application. You create an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) group named **Cosmos DB Creators** to allow provisioning of Azure Cosmos accounts, databases, and containers.  
  
The Azure AD group must be unable to access the keys required to access the data.  
  
You need to limit access for the Azure AD group.  
  
Which role-based access control should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Cosmos DB Operator role allows management of Azure Cosmos DB accounts without access to the data, account keys, or connection strings. It therefore supports provisioning and management while preventing the group from obtaining the keys needed to access data.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles)

You develop and deploy a web application to Azure App Service. The application accesses data stored in an Azure Storage account. The account has several containers containing several blobs with large volumes of data. You deploy all Azure resources in a single region.  
  
You need to move the Azure Storage account to a new region and must copy all data to that region.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Export the Azure Storage account Azure Resource Manager template
Configure object replication for all blobs
Use the AzCopy command line tool
Create a new Azure Storage account in the current region
Create a new subscription in the current region

questions.explanation:
Azure Storage account relocation begins by exporting the source account’s Azure Resource Manager template. The template is then modified with a new account name and target region and deployed to create the destination account; the blob data can subsequently be copied, such as with AzCopy. [Relocate Azure Storage Account to another region — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/relocation/relocation-storage-account)

**Learn more:** [Relocate Azure Storage Account to another region](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/relocation/relocation-storage-account)

You must ensure that the security policies are satisfied.  
  
Which code should you add at line CS07 in `ConfigureSSE.ps1`?
questions.explanation:
Customer-managed encryption uses an Azure Key Vault key to wrap and unwrap the account encryption key. The service identity therefore requires the Key Vault key permissions `get`, `wrapkey`, and `unwrapkey`; certificate permissions and `encrypt`/`decrypt` are not the required access-policy permissions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Customer-managed keys for account encryption — Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a REST API in Azure App Service.  
  
The API must be invoked by an Azure App Service web app, and it must retrieve and update user profile information stored in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
You need to configure the API so that it can perform the updates.  
  
Which two tools should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Graph API provides the endpoints and permissions for reading and updating Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) user profiles. Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) acquires the Azure AD access tokens the application needs to call Microsoft Graph with those permissions.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart - Edit profile in a sample Node.js web app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-web-app-node-sign-in-edit-profile) · [Acquire and cache tokens with Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/msal/msal-acquire-cache-tokens)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a B2B web application that uses Azure B2B collaboration for authentication. Paying customers authenticate to Azure B2B by using federation.  
  
The application lets users register trial accounts with any email address.  
  
When a user becomes a paying customer, the data associated with the trial must be retained, but the user must authenticate through federation.  
  
You need to update the user in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) when the user converts to a paying customer.  
  
Which Graph API parameter is used to switch authentication from one-time passcodes to federation?
questions.explanation:
The `resetRedemption` property resets an existing B2B guest user's invitation redemption and reinvites that same user while preserving the user object ID, group memberships, and application assignments. The user can then redeem the new invitation through the applicable federated identity provider.

**Learn more:** [Invitation resource type - Microsoft Graph v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/invitation?view=graph-rest-1.0) · [Reset guest redemption status - Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/reset-redemption-status)

A company is building a solution that enables smart refrigerators to send temperature data to a central location.  
  
The solution must receive and retain messages until they can be processed. You create an Azure Service Bus instance by specifying a name, pricing tier, subscription, resource group, and location.  
  
You need to finish the configuration.  
  
Which Azure CLI or PowerShell command should you run?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Service Bus queue provides durable message storage until a receiving application processes the messages. After creating the Service Bus namespace, create the queue with `az servicebus queue create`, specifying its resource group, namespace name, and queue name. Microsoft’s Azure CLI quickstart uses this command sequence to create a namespace and then a queue.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart - Use the Azure CLI to create a Service Bus queue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-quickstart-cli) · [az servicebus queue - Azure CLI reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/servicebus/queue?view=azure-cli-latest)

questions.question:
Solution: Use the .NET API for the mobile application to add a message to an Azure Service Bus Queue. Create an Azure Windows VM that is triggered by the Azure Service Bus Queue.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus requires session-enabled entities and session identifiers to guarantee FIFO processing. Azure Functions provides the native Service Bus queue trigger; an always-provisioned Windows VM is not a Service Bus-triggered serverless consumer and incurs cost during periods with no messages. Therefore, this design does not satisfy the FIFO and cost-minimization requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus quotas and limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-quotas) · [Azure Service Bus trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-service-bus-trigger)

questions.question:
Solution: Use the .NET API from the mobile application to add a message to an Azure Storage Queue. Create an Azure VM that is triggered by Azure Storage Queue events.  
  
Does the solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Queue does not guarantee first-in-first-out message delivery; its individual queue capacity can also reach 500 TiB, so it does not enforce an 80 GB maximum queue size. The solution therefore fails the FIFO and queue-size requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Queue Storage REST API — Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/queue-service-rest-api) · [Scalability and performance targets for Queue Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/queues/scalability-targets)

questions.question:
Solution: Use the .NET API to add a message from the mobile application to an Azure Service Bus Queue. Create an Azure Function App that uses an Azure Service Bus Queue trigger.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Service Bus queues provide durable FIFO message delivery and decouple senders from consumers. An Azure Function with a Service Bus trigger runs in response to queued messages, which suits intermittent traffic and avoids the need for continuously running processing infrastructure. Configuring the queue's size below 80 GB satisfies the queue-size constraint.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus queues, topics, and subscriptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-queues-topics-subscriptions) · [Azure Service Bus trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-service-bus-trigger)

questions.question:
Solution: Use the .NET API from the mobile application to add a message to an Azure Storage Queue. Create an Azure Function App that uses an Azure Storage Queue trigger.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Azure Storage Queues do not provide guaranteed FIFO message delivery or processing. Therefore, an Azure Storage Queue trigger cannot meet a requirement for FIFO message ordering.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an Azure-based web application. The application periodically goes offline to carry out offline data processing. While it is offline, many Azure Monitor alerts fire and page the on-call developer.  
  
The application must always log whenever it is offline for any reason.  
  
You need to prevent the on-call developer from being paged during offline processing.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add Azure Monitor alert processing rules to suppress notifications.
Disable Azure Monitor Service Health Alerts during offline processing.
Create an Azure Monitor Metric Alert.
Build an Azure Monitor action group that suppresses the alerts.

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor alert processing rules can suppress notifications for fired alerts during a defined maintenance or offline-processing window. Suppression removes the affected alerts’ action groups, so paging does not occur, while the alerts still fire and remain visible in Azure Monitor for logging and review.

**Learn more:** [Alert processing rules for Azure Monitor alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-processing-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You develop a solution that uses Azure Virtual Machines (VMs).  
  
The VMs host code that must access resources in an Azure resource group. You grant the VM access to the resource group in Resource Manager.  
  
You need to obtain an access token that uses the VM's system-assigned managed identity.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: From the code on the VM, call Azure Resource Manager using an access token.
Use PowerShell on a remote machine to make a request to the local managed identity for Azure resources endpoint.
Use PowerShell on the VM to make a request to the local managed identity for Azure resources endpoint.
From the code on the VM, call Azure Resource Manager using a SAS token.
From the code on the VM, generate a user delegation SAS token.

questions.explanation:
A VM’s system-assigned managed identity requests an Azure Resource Manager token from the local Azure Instance Metadata Service managed-identity endpoint. The returned token is a bearer access token that code running on the VM uses when calling Azure Resource Manager. The endpoint is available only from within that VM, so the token request must run on the VM rather than on a remote machine.

**Learn more:** [How to use managed identities for Azure resources on an Azure VM to acquire an access token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-to-use-vm-token) · [How managed identities for Azure resources work with Azure virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-managed-identities-work-vm)

You need to address the log-capacity issue.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an Application Insights Telemetry Filter
Change the minimum log level in the host.json file for the function

questions.explanation:
Application Insights sampling reduces telemetry volume during high activity, helping stay within telemetry ingestion and storage capacity while retaining representative monitoring data. Azure Functions supports Application Insights sampling configuration in `host.json`.\
\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to deploy several Azure virtual machines to the subscription by using Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates. The virtual machines will be included in one availability set.  
  
You need to ensure that the ARM template enables as many virtual machines as possible to remain accessible during a fabric failure or maintenance event.  
  
Which value should you configure for the `platformFaultDomainCount` property?
questions.explanation:
Fault domains group virtual machines that share a common power source and network switch. Configuring the maximum supported fault-domain count spreads virtual machines across the greatest number of fault domains, reducing the number affected by a single fabric failure. Availability-set maintenance is also isolated by update domains, but `platformFaultDomainCount` specifically controls fault-domain distribution.

**Learn more:** [Availability sets overview - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/availability-set-overview) · [az vm availability-set create](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/vm/availability-set?view=azure-cli-latest)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing several APIs hosted by Azure API Management (APIM).  
  
You must transform the APIs to conceal private backend information and obscure the technology stack used for backend processing.  
  
You need to protect all APIs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure and apply a new inbound policy scoped to a product.
Configure and apply a new outbound policy scoped to the operation.
Configure and apply a new outbound policy scoped to global.
Configure and apply a new backend policy scoped to global.

questions.explanation:
Response transformations that remove or alter headers and other backend-revealing details are applied in the outbound policy section before the response is returned to the caller. A global APIM policy scope applies to All APIs in the APIM instance, so it protects every hosted API consistently.

**Learn more:** [Set or edit Azure API Management policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/set-edit-policies) · [Azure API Management policy reference - forward request](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/forward-request-policy)

You require alerts for any unusual increase in the rate of failed HTTP requests directed at App1.  
  
You need to implement push notifications.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Azure portal, modify diagnostic settings of AppInsights1.
Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures AppInsights1.
Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures the analyticsItems child resource of AppInsights1.
Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that modifies an action group.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
An organization deploys Azure Cosmos DB.  
  
You need to ensure that the index is updated when items are created, updated, or deleted.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set the indexing mode to Lazy.
Set the value of the automatic property of the indexing policy to False.
Set the value of the EnableScanInQuery option to True.
Set the indexing mode to Consistent.

questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB’s **Consistent** indexing mode updates the index synchronously as items are created, updated, or deleted. Lazy indexing performs lower-priority asynchronous updates and can produce temporarily incomplete results.\
\
**Learn more:** [Indexing policies - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/index-policy)
